title: Kevin and Jack Sinfield face diverging paths to Super League Grand Final
content:
The Sinfield family is set to feature in the Super League Grand Final, with father Kevin and son Jack pursuing diverging paths to the title match. While Leeds has served as the focal point of their rugby story for over 20 years, attention has shifted 10 miles to Wakefield this week as Jack aims to secure his first title with the Wakefield Trinity Wildcats.

title: Guardiola backs Manchester City owners after guilty verdict on financial rules
content:
Pep Guardiola has voiced his support for Manchester City following the club’s guilty verdict on all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period. The former manager, who left the club in the summer after a decade in charge, told fans, “We will get through this together,” while adding, “I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club.”

Guardiola’s first two seasons at Manchester City fell within the timeframe investigated by the independent commission. He remains a close ally of chief executive Ferran Soriano, who brought him to England, as the two previously worked together at Barcelona.

Despite the verdict, Manchester City maintains its innocence and is set to appeal against the decision before Friday’s deadline. Former City chair Bernstein has called on directors to quit in response to the outcome.
summary: Pep Guardiola expressed his continued support for Manchester City after the club was found guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period. The club maintains its innocence and is set to appeal against the decision before Friday's deadline.

title: TIGEM study identifies druggable pathway to activate TFEB for lysosomal diseases
content:
A study published in Nature by scientists at the Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine (TIGEM) has identified a molecular pathway that regulates TFEB activity. This discovery reveals new druggable targets that could facilitate the development of therapies for conditions linked to lysosomal dysfunction, including rare genetic diseases and cancer.

TFEB has long been considered a promising therapeutic target for restoring the cell’s ability to clear and recycle waste. However, translating this potential into actual treatments has been challenging because TFEB itself is difficult to target with drugs. The newly identified pathway offers a route to overcome this obstacle by providing alternative molecular targets for intervention.
summary: A study by TIGEM scientists published in Nature identified a molecular pathway that controls TFEB activity, providing new druggable targets. These targets could enable therapies for rare genetic diseases, cancer, and other conditions linked to lysosomal dysfunction.

content:

The research examines how different patterns of parenting relate to these issues, noting that there is no single correct way to raise a child.

The study categorizes the observed problems into two main groups: internalizing behaviors, such as withdrawal, anxiety, and depression, and externalizing behaviors, including aggression, oppositional behavior, and attention problems.

content:

The technology is designed to monitor these changes throughout the rehabilitation process.

By providing continuous data, the device could enable clinicians to adjust therapy in real time. This approach aims to tailor patient care rather than relying on the current one-size-fits-all method.
summary: Researchers at the University of Massachusetts Amherst created a wearable wrist device that uses a machine-learning algorithm to track arm movement impairment after a stroke. title: Ocean heatwaves are hiding months of extra warming
content:
Marine heatwaves represent only the peak intensity of broader warming events, as elevated ocean temperatures often persist for months beyond the initial peak. This extended duration means that traditional monitoring methods fail to capture the full scope of thermal stress experienced by marine environments.

Recent research indicates that conventional measurements underestimate total heat exposure by an average of more than 150%. By ignoring the lingering warmth after the main event, these standard metrics overlook a significant source of stress on marine ecosystems.
summary: Marine heatwaves may be only the most intense part of much longer warming events, with elevated temperatures sometimes lingering for months. Researchers found that conventional measurements underestimate total heat exposure by more than 150% on average, potentially overlooking a major source of stress on marine ecosystems.

content:

title: Strata: New Semantic Layer Simplifies LLM Integration
content:
Ajo, who spent four years at Netflix working on self-service solutions for non-technical business users, has introduced Strata, an expressive semantic layer designed to work with large language models. The full-stack solution includes dashboards, subscriptions, and Google Sheets exports, accessible via view agent conversations or Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Key features of Strata include strict naming conventions that ensure only one entity, such as "Revenue," exists per project, enabling automatic data blending across fact domains. The system utilizes partition and aggregate-aware semantic routing to select faster compute engines like Druid or ClickHouse for specific queries while retaining full history in cheaper engines like Trino. Additional capabilities include out-of-the-box support for complex measures like snapshots, LOD, and compound measures, as well as the ability to create custom calculations and apply cohorts as filters.

Strata is currently in early beta and is not open source, though it offers a free tier supporting up to 25 users that can be run locally via Docker. The developer explicitly states they are not building a semantic layer for traditional BI tools, instead providing APIs and MCP for custom integrations.
summary: Ajo, who spent four years at Netflix building self‑service tools for non‑technical users, built Strata, a full‑stack semantic layer that balances expressiveness and ease of use and works well with LLMs. Strata offers dashboards, subscriptions, Google Sheets exports, strict naming conventions, automatic data blending, tiered compute routing, complex measures, custom calculations, cohort filtering, and can be accessed via agent conversation or via MCP, and is available as an early beta that is not open source but includes a free tier for up to 25 users that can run on Docker.

title: Parrot: Open-Source Smart Meeting Recorder with Co-Pilot for Mac
content:
Uygar, an entrepreneur based in London, has released Parrot, an open-source smart meeting recorder designed for Mac. Developed over several months with the assistance of Claude, the tool was originally created to address his personal need for better memory retention during daily business calls with customers, partners, and suppliers.

The application records audio from the Mac and keeps all data stored locally on the user's computer when using local models, requiring no account creation or API calls. Parrot features a "copilot" function that allows users to upload files; when the software detects related questions during a meeting, it recommends answers from those files. Users can also connect their own Claude API and Deepgram accounts to enhance the tool's capabilities, though this option involves making external API calls.

title: Magnitude (YC S25) Launches Self-Optimizing Inference Engine for Local Agents
content:
Launch HN: Magnitude (YC S25) – Self‑optimizing inference engine for agents

Anders and Tom, software engineers who previously built an open‑source browser agent with 4,000+ GitHub stars and 100,000+ downloads, have announced Magnitude, a new inference engine that automatically tunes itself to run as fast as possible on a user’s hardware. The engine supports Mac, Linux, and Windows on any hardware and claims to be up to twice as fast as llama.cpp.

Magnitude is designed for local agent workloads, offering on‑device kernel compilation and tuning, focus on popular open‑weight families, dynamic memory allocation that grows only as needed, and hybrid paged attention that shares prefix caches without sacrificing single‑session speed. Benchmarks with the Qwen 3.6 35B A3B (4‑bit) model show a 92 % faster decode on a Mac M4 Pro (30 tok/s → 57 tok/s) and a 19 % faster decode on a DGX Spark GPU (49 tok/s → 58 tok/s), along with 27–28 % less per‑agent memory usage.

The project is fully open source under the Apache 2.0 license, built in Rust with a custom GPU kernel runtime and autotuner. Future plans include expert streaming, a kernel compiler for automatic fusion, and multi‑device utilization. The team invites users to try the desktop app, connect it to agents such as Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, and Codex, and provide feedback via the comments link.
summary: Magnitude is an open-source inference engine built in Rust that optimizes itself for specific hardware to run local agents up to 2x faster than llama.cpp. It features dynamic memory allocation and hybrid paged attention to allow concurrent sessions without sacrificing single-session performance.

title: A Biotech Founder Makes the Moral Case for Gene-Editing Human Embryos
content:
Origin Genomics founder Cathy Tie has framed gene‑editing of human embryos as a “moral imperative” for combating hereditary diseases, despite the practice’s ongoing controversy and associated risks.  

Tie’s argument underscores her belief that the technology should be pursued to prevent genetic disorders, even as the scientific community continues to debate its safety and ethical implications.
summary: The practice of editing the genes of embryos remains highly controversial and risky, but Origin Genomics founder Cathy Tie argues its a “moral imperative” to address hereditary diseases.

title: Wing Hummingbird 7000W‑B drone delivers potatoes
content:
Potato by air

A new delivery drone, the Wing Hummingbird 7000W‑B, has been used to ship potatoes across a local neighborhood. The drone weighs less than 15 pounds and is equipped with 16 propellers—four for horizontal movement and 12 for vertical lift. It can reach a top speed of 60 miles per hour, carry up to 2.7 pounds, and deliver within a radius of about six miles. The Federal Aviation Administration has authorized it for beyond‑line‑of‑sight piloting.

The author first learned of the drone when neighbor Will added him and a half dozen other local dads to a group chat a few Sunday mornings ago. The author has mainly used the drone to send potatoes to people in the area. The post was shared on Instagram and the full story is available on The Verge.
summary: The Wing Hummingbird 7000W‑B delivery drone weighs less than 15 pounds and can carry up to 2.7 pounds at a top speed of 60 miles per hour. It has 16 propellers, a delivery radius of about six miles, is FAA‑authorized for beyond‑line‑of‑sight piloting, and has been used to send potatoes to people.

title: Sonos Ace Ultra: Improved Design, Sound, and App Fixes Over Original Ace
content:
Sonos has released the Ace Ultra headphones, which maintain the same exterior design as the original Ace model but offer improved internal performance. The initial Ace headphones were intended to be a strong entry into the category but were overshadowed by a poorly received app redesign. While the original models were noted for their build quality, sound, and comfort, they suffered from significant functional limitations.

The primary feature of the original Ace headphones allowed users to reroute audio from a Sonos soundbar to the headphones. However, this functionality was initially glitchy and restricted to compatibility with the $1,000 Arc soundbar and only one pair of headphones at a time. Sonos has since fixed these specific issues, though the original models still could not connect to the rest of the system.
summary: The Sonos Ace Ultra headphones resemble the original Ace but offer improved internal features. The original Ace's flagship audio‑rerouting feature was glitchy, worked only with the $1,000 Arc soundbar, and supported only one pair of headphones at launch, but those issues have now been fixed.

title: Amazon's Fire TV Stick 4K Now Powers Directly from TV USB
content:
Amazon has announced a new Fire TV Stick 4K that no longer requires a separate power adapter. The device can be powered directly from a TV’s USB port, making setup easier than earlier 4K sticks.

The new stick is available today for $59.99 and runs on Amazon’s refreshed TV OS. It includes Wi‑Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, and Bluetooth Low Energy connectivity.  

Amazon is also simplifying its streaming‑stick lineup, now offering four models instead of five: the Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K, Fire TV Stick 4K Max, and Fire TV Cube.

title: Instagram Adds AI Assistant to Provide Post Feedback
content:
Instagram announced on Wednesday that its standalone Edits app will now include an AI “creative assistant” that pulls data from a user’s Instagram account to offer suggestions on how to improve posts.  

The assistant lets creators ask open‑ended questions such as what’s trending on Instagram, why one video performed better than another, or which content resonated most with their audience. It uses metrics from the account—including likes, views, video retention, and shares—to generate its feedback.  

According to Instagram, the tool can spot patterns in a creator’s performance data to help guide future content decisions.
summary: Instagram announced that its standalone Edits app will now include an AI “creative assistant” that pulls data from a user’s Instagram account and offers suggestions on what to change. The assistant can answer open‑ended questions about trending content and uses metrics such as likes, views, retention on videos, and shares.

title: Google Tests Paying Publishers for AI Search Contributions
content:
Google has launched a pilot program that pays publishers for their contributions to its AI‑powered search features, according to a report from The Information. The pilot, which began less than a year ago, reportedly includes around 100 publishers and is part of Google’s response to scrutiny over how its AI features affect web traffic.

Under the test, Google is paying participating publishers based on how much their content is used in AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search, as well as in its Gemini chatbot. Digiday first reported on the pilot program, and one publisher that joined when it started earned over $1 million.

The program’s details were first disclosed by Digiday.
summary: Google has launched a pilot program that pays publishers for how much their content contributes to its AI Overviews, AI Mode in Search, and Gemini chatbot. The pilot involves around 100 publishers and began less than a year ago.

title: Meta Launches Muse AI Agent with New Features and Security Patch
content:
Meta has unveiled Muse, a new AI agent that claims to assist users with tasks ranging from sending emails to making online purchases. The company says Muse can perform these functions effectively, provided users are willing to share personal data and credit card information with the platform.

Muse’s capabilities extend beyond basic tasks. Meta has made the agent’s filesystem more accessible, allowing users to download its entire contents, and plans to add video‑chat functionality. The company is also developing a Tamagotchi‑style Muse Charm device that will not include Instagram integration but can interact with other Muse Charms. In addition, Muse is slated for integration with Meta smart glasses and a standalone gadget, and the platform’s Enterprise version will bring Muse AI tools to small businesses.

The launch has sparked security concerns, as Muse was reported to have sent a YouTuber’s address to a stranger and an exploit that could let attackers control the agent. Meta patched the vulnerability, but Amazon has blocked the Muse AI agent, and Mark Zuckerberg has urged users to trust the system. Muse now also has a Mac app, and Meta continues to position the agent as a key player in its AI strategy.
summary: Meta launched Muse AI, an agent that can send emails and handle online purchases, and has added new features such as a Muse Charm device and a Mac app. The company also patched a security exploit that allowed attackers to control the AI agent.

title: Halide Camera App Adds Full Aperture Control for iPhone 18 Pro
content:

The update gives users more precise control than the native iOS camera, which limits aperture adjustments to just four presets. Third‑party apps such as BlackMagic Camera and Moment Pro Camera II already expand that to 10 presets in 1/3‑stop increments, similar to most digital cameras.  

Halide Mark III goes even further by offering additional aperture control, although the exact details are not included in the brief.  

Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: The latest update to Lux Optics' Halide camera app adds two new photography looks and full support for the variable aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro’s main camera. Halide provides more granular aperture control than other third‑party apps, surpassing the four presets of the native iOS camera.

content:

title: Appeals court pauses execution of Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike
content:
A U.S. appeals court issued a short stay of execution for death‑row inmate Christa Pike less than two hours before she was slated to receive a lethal injection. The halt came as the state prepared to carry out what would have been the first execution of a woman in Tennessee in more than two centuries.

The court’s order pauses the scheduled execution to allow judges time to review Pike’s claim that her history of severe sexual abuse was not considered during her sentencing. Pike’s attorneys argue that the abuse should have been a mitigating factor in the case.

The stay delays the state’s attempt to carry out the execution while the appellate court evaluates the presented arguments.
summary: A US appeals court ordered a short stay of execution for death row inmate Christa Pike less than two hours before she was scheduled to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than two centuries. The court halted the execution to consider Pike's claims that her history of severe sexual abuse was not taken into account during sentencing.

title: France 24 reporter gains exclusive access to Uyghur fighters in Syrian forces
content:
Foreign fighters played a role in the ousting of Syria’s President Bashar al‑Assad nearly two years ago, with Uyghur combatants among the groups credited for the effort. The Uyghurs are a predominantly Muslim, Turkic ethnic minority that lives across Central Asia, particularly in China’s Xinjiang region.

After the conflict’s turning point, Uyghur fighters grew into one of the largest foreign‑fighter contingents in Syria, though those who remain and have established lives there are known for keeping a low profile. 

France 24 journalist Wassim Nasr recently traveled to Syria and obtained exclusive access to the Uyghur fighters, providing a rare glimpse into their integration within local armed forces.
summary: Uyghur fighters, a Turkic Muslim minority from Central Asia, became one of the largest foreign‑fighter groups that helped topple Bashar al‑Assad about two years ago. France 24 journalist Wassim Nasr recently visited Syria and obtained exclusive access to those Uyghur fighters.

title: Copernicus Ocean State Report says climate change reshapes polar oceans
content:
An annual report released on Wednesday warned that climate change is increasingly reshaping the polar oceans. The Copernicus Ocean State Report noted rapid warming of Arctic waters, a reduction in sea‑ice extent and loss of wildlife habitat at both the Arctic and Antarctic ends of the planet.

The report also highlighted broader oceanic impacts, describing record‑breaking heatwaves in the Mediterranean and Black seas. It documented shifts in marine ecosystems and a trend toward increasingly acidic waters across the world’s seas.

These findings underscore profound changes occurring throughout the global ocean system, according to the Copernicus Ocean State Report.
summary: The annual Copernicus Ocean State Report said Wednesday that climate change is rapidly reshaping the polar oceans, with Arctic waters warming, sea ice shrinking, and wildlife losing habitat. It also notes record‑breaking heatwaves in the Mediterranean and Black Seas, shifts in marine ecosystems and increasingly acidic waters worldwide.
author: France 24

title: Gov. Kathy Hochul calls for probe of Cornell's handling of 2024 gang rape claim
content:

The governor’s call coincides with prosecutors reopening their own inquiry into the alleged rape, citing claims that the elite college did not adequately punish the men involved.
summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul on Tuesday called for an investigation into Cornell University's response to a 2024 gang rape allegation. Prosecutors have reopened the investigation after claims the college failed to properly punish the seven students accused.

title: Israel PM Netanyahu says pilot tried to crash Tel Aviv‑bound flydubai after Saudi landing
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that the pilot of a Tel Aviv‑bound flydubai flight deliberately tried to crash the aircraft and kill its passengers after the plane was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.  

Passengers on the flight corroborated the claim, reporting a struggle for control when the aircraft suddenly dropped about 17,000 feet in roughly one minute, according to data from the Flightradar24 website.
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilot of a Tel Aviv‑bound flydubai flight tried to crash the plane and kill its passengers after the aircraft was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. content:
London announced on Wednesday that the United Kingdom and France have scrapped their “one in, one out” migrant exchange pilot. The agreement, which was intended to curb the number of people attempting to cross the English Channel in small boats, will no longer be pursued.

The pilot programme aimed to break the business model of people smugglers by swapping undocumented migrants who had made the crossing for individuals who had applied for asylum through legal channels.
summary: London said on Wednesday that the British‑French agreement to reduce English Channel small‑boat crossings has been scrapped. The pilot programme was designed to exchange undocumented migrants who crossed the Channel for individuals who had applied for asylum legally.

content:

The country will only take those who are not accused of crime or terrorism links, according to Nancy Ninette Mutoni, a spokesperson for President Évariste Ndayishimiye. Mutoni made the statement in a Tuesday announcement.

summary: Burundi has agreed to join other African nations in receiving migrants deported from the United States under Donald Trump’s immigration policy, spokesperson Nancy Ninette Mutoni said. content:

summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa said men must take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced new measures to address the recent wave of murders. summary: The captain and first officer on the Flydubai flight to Israel were injured in a stabbing. Officials said one pilot has been arrested.

title: SKF advert review – let’s hope this dull AI Greta Garbo is not the future
content: Swedish-American actor Greta Garbo has been the subject of a recent review of an SKF advertisement, which the source describes as a "bizarre, humourless" 99-second spot. The article characterizes the use of the actor’s image as a "dull AI Greta Garbo," suggesting it provides another reason to resent AI. The piece notes that Garbo had previously faced what is described as a final indignity in life: a 1970 television sketch by Peter Cook and Dudley Moore. In that sketch, Pete portrayed the legendary recluse standing on the back of a flatbed truck, shouting "I vant to be alone!" at city crowds through a megaphone.
summary: Swedish-American actor exhumed for bizarre, humourless 99 seconds that give us another reason to resent AIPoor Greta Garbo. Perhaps, in life, she thought her final indignity would be the Peter Cook and Dudley Moore TV sketch from 1970, showing Pete as the legendary recluse standing on the back of a flatbed truck as it rumbles through the crowded city streets, shouting at everyone through a megaphone: “I vant to be alone!” Continue reading...

title: Manchester City CEO Soriano calls guilty verdicts a 'Premier League conspiracy theory'
content:
Ferran Soriano, chief executive of Manchester City, has dismissed the recent guilty verdicts against the club as a “Premier League conspiracy theory” rooted in “a single false accusation.” In a video message sent to staff, Soriano maintained the club’s innocence and announced that Manchester City intends to appeal the decision.

The independent panel concluded that Manchester City artificially inflated revenue and reduced costs by more than £900m over a nine-year period. The ruling stated that this was achieved through “sham” sponsorship deals primarily funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), the club’s owner.

Soriano confirmed the club’s intention to fight the case following the guilty verdict on more than 100 charges, which was officially confirmed on Tuesday.
summary: Ferran Soriano stated that the guilty verdicts against Manchester City are based on a single false accusation and a Premier League conspiracy theory. The club confirmed it will appeal the verdicts, which found the club artificially inflated revenue by more than £900m over nine years.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wiegman drops Kelly and Toone for Greece playoff over club form
content:
Sarina Wiegman, England’s coach, has excluded Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly from the squad for the October playoff against Greece, citing performance levels that did not meet her expectations. Wiegman stated unequivocally that the main reason for their omission was that their on-pitch levels were not what she expected from them.

The decision serves as a wake-up call to the entire squad, sending a message that players must perform for their clubs to secure a spot in the World Cup. By leaving out two heroes from 2022 and 2025, Wiegman used her typically honest and straight-to-the-point style to emphasize that reputation is irrelevant without the required performance standard.
summary: England coach Sarina Wiegman left out Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly from the squad for the October playoff against Greece. She stated that their on-pitch levels did not meet her expectations, using the decision as a warning to the entire squad to perform for their clubs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tuchel praises Alexander-Arnold for decisive display in England win over Czechia
content:
Thomas Tuchel praised Trent Alexander-Arnold for a “decisive” performance following the right-back’s first England appearance since June 2025. Alexander-Arnold, who had previously missed out on a World Cup spot, was highlighted as a key positive for the team as they recovered from their earlier defeat to Spain.

The England side recorded a comfortable 2-0 victory away to Czechia in the Nations League on Tuesday. Alexander-Arnold set up the opening goal in the match, contributing significantly to the team's success. Tuchel noted that the squad needs to remain focused, adding that Alexander-Arnold was a big help in securing the win.
summary: Thomas Tuchel praised Trent Alexander-Arnold for his performance in England's 2-0 Nations League win away to Czechia. Alexander-Arnold set up the opening goal in his first appearance for the team since June 2025.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Next Generation 2021: Early breakthrough does not guarantee future success
content:
The 2021 Next Generation series, which tracked 80 players including 20 from the Premier League and 60 from elsewhere, demonstrates that early breakthroughs do not ensure long-term success or longevity in world football. While predicting trajectories is difficult, recent updates highlight the rapid rise of Lamine Yamal, who was identified in 2024.

Yamal, a ball-playing central midfielder, comes from a prominent footballing family where tactical awareness is deeply rooted. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and currently manages Worthing FC, while his great-uncle Martin, grandfather Paul, and great-grandfather Wally all had playing careers.

The midfielder has set multiple records, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day. He subsequently became the youngest player in the Champions League 17 days later, the youngest Bundesliga goal scorer 11 days after that, and the youngest player and goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before turning 17.
summary: A review of the 2021 Next Generation class shows that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success. The article highlights Lamine Yamal, noting he is from a footballing family and holds several age records in the Bundesliga and Champions League.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Peter O’Mahony discusses retirement, gardening, and criticism of coaches
content:
Former Ireland, Munster, and Lions captain Peter O’Mahony has opened up about his transition into his second year of retirement, reflecting on how his previous "taciturn grit and uncompromising commitment" have been replaced by more complex reflections. Speaking from Dublin, O’Mahony discussed the challenge of overcoming a "deep-down hatred" of losing that once caused despair and derailed his performance, noting that the natural instinct not to lose sometimes got in his way.

The former captain also shared his views on his coaching experiences, stating that every coach he had was "a bit mad" with the exception of Andy Farrell. O’Mahony described the pain associated with his "ruthless exit" from Munster, while acknowledging the necessity of personal change. He added that he is now enjoying gardening, a hobby that contrasts sharply with the hard-edged ritual of his playing career.
summary: Former Ireland captain Peter O’Mahony reflects on his second year of retirement, noting a shift from competitive grit to complex personal reflections. He discusses his love of gardening and claims that every coach except Andy Farrell has been 'a bit mad'.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Japan Takes T20 World Champions India To Final Ball In Historic Cricket Clash
content:
Japan, ranked 41st in the world, took T20 world champions India to the final ball in a historic cricket match that was nearly derailed by Typhoon Dujuan. The intense contest concluded with Axar Patel delivering a dot ball, securing a victory for India after a tense finish that saw Japanese batter Alexander Shirai-Patmore and his teammates come perilously close to a major upset.

The match was part of a brief meeting between the cricketing minnows and giants, which had earlier faced disruption from the typhoon. Japan’s performance highlighted the significant gap between the teams while demonstrating the competitive potential of the lower-ranked side against the illustrious visitors.
summary: Japan, ranked 41st in the world, forced T20 world champions India to the final ball in a match that was nearly disrupted by Typhoon Dujuan. Axar Patel bowled the final delivery for a dot ball, preventing a major upset by the Japanese team.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester City to pay Premier League up to £50m in legal costs after guilty verdict
content:
Manchester City is expected to owe the Premier League up to £50 million in legal costs after an independent commission found the club guilty of breaking financial rules. The Premier League announced on Tuesday that the panel determined the club had artificially inflated its income by £900 million over a nine-year period.

The commission concluded that Manchester City arranged “sham” contracts to boost revenues in order to comply with spending regulations. The club denies wrongdoing, describing the allegations as a “conspiracy theory.”
summary: An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of artificially inflating income by £900m over nine years using sham contracts. The club denies wrongdoing, calling the allegations a conspiracy theory, but is set to owe the Premier League tens of millions in legal costs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ben Stokes finishes county summer with Durham, England contract ends
content:
Ben Stokes has concluded his county summer with Durham, marking the end of his England central contract. The period was described as tumultuous, ultimately ending in success for the cricketer.

The situation now leaves questions regarding what is in store for Stokes as he moves forward.
summary: Ben Stokes finished the county summer playing for Durham. His England central contract has ended.

title: Premier League's Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Taiwo Awoniyi study to become sporting directors
content:
Premier League footballers are pursuing academic qualifications to prepare for roles as sporting directors while still playing professionally.  

Kiernan Dewsbury‑Hall, Taiwo Awoniyi and other players have been balancing their football commitments with study, even using the team bus on away trips to attend classes.  

They continue to juggle education alongside their football careers.
summary: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Taiwo Awoniyi and other Premier League players are pursuing education while playing football. They have been studying on the team bus during away trips.

title: Pritzker Loses 80 Pounds with GLP-1, Sparking Debate on Presidential Appearance
content:
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, a Democrat who is considering a 2028 presidential run, has lost 80 pounds over the past two years. The governor acknowledged the change, attributing the weight loss to the use of a GLP-1 medication prescribed to help treat his diabetes.

The significant physical transformation has become apparent in recent months, prompting a broader discussion regarding shifting public attitudes toward the appearance of presidential candidates.
summary: JB Pritzker, Illinois Democratic governor, has lost 80 pounds in the last two years using a GLP‑1 to treat diabetes. His weight loss has been so apparent in recent months that it has sparked discussion about changing attitudes toward presidential appearance.

title: Republicans in both chambers break ranks with Trump on multiple issues
content:
Republicans in both chambers of Congress are increasingly breaking ranks with President Trump on multiple sensitive issues. The party members hope that establishing some separation from the GOP’s unpopular standard bearer will help prevent a blue wave in the upcoming midterm elections.

These divisions are described as highly unusual for a political party that has previously walked virtually in lock-step with Trump for more than a decade.
summary: Republicans in both chambers are increasingly breaking ranks with President Trump across a host of sensitive issues. The divisions are highly unusual for a party that has walked virtually in lock‑step with Trump.

title: Trump administration faces deadline to spend unspent healthcare funding
content:
Unspent healthcare funding faces a do‑or‑die cliff as the fiscal year ends on Wednesday. The Trump administration has refused to spend billions of dollars that Congress appropriated for health programs, putting those funds at risk of expiration.

Democratic lawmakers and some Republicans have called the administration’s refusal illegal. The move has become a significant test of Congress’s willingness to confront the Trump administration over the use of appropriated funds.
summary: The Trump administration has refused to spend billions of dollars appropriated by Congress for health programs. These funds are at risk of expiring on Wednesday when the fiscal year ends.

title: Brookings confirms basic economics predictions about Biden’s open border
content:
Brookings confirms what basic economics predicted about Biden’s open border.  

The Biden administration ran an unhedged book for four years. The results were higher rents, suppressed wages at the low end of the distribution, school systems absorbing students they hadn’t budgeted for, and emergency rooms eating uncompensated care.
summary: The Biden administration ran an unhedged book for four years. The outcome included higher rents, suppressed low‑end wages, schools absorbing unbudgeted students, and emergency rooms covering uncompensated care.

content:

title: President Trump says top tech firms signed accord to self‑police AI development
content: President Trump said on Tuesday that he and a large group of leaders of artificial intelligence companies had signed a voluntary accord. The agreement, according to Trump, will include both internal and external reviews. The accord is described as a means for top tech firms to self‑police AI development.
summary: President Trump said on Tuesday that he and a large group of leaders of artificial intelligence companies had signed a voluntary accord. The accord will include internal and external reviews.

title: Outside groups spend $50M on New Hampshire Senate race that could decide Congress control
content:
Outside groups are pouring millions into Senate races that could decide Congress’s control next year.  

New Hampshire’s Senate contest is highlighted as one of the few races that could tip the balance of power in the Senate.  

To date, outside money groups have invested roughly $50 million in the New Hampshire race.
summary: Outside money groups have invested about $50 million in New Hampshire's Senate race. The race could decide control of Congress next year.

title: HHS Claims Gender-Affirming Care May Radicalize Transgender Patients
content: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has released a report that claims gender‑affirming care may radicalize individuals. The report is described as the agency’s latest effort to chip away at trust in established health‑care models for transgender people. Critics argue that the report frames transgender identity as illegitimate or even dangerous.
summary: The report is the agency's latest effort to chip away at trust in established health care models for transgender people. Critics say it frames transgender identity as illegitimate or even dangerous.

title: Jack Smith Defends Two Trump Indictments on Capitol Hill
content:
Former Justice Department special counsel Jack Smith defended two criminal indictments against President Trump on Capitol Hill.

Smith’s remarks were made during a congressional hearing where the indictments were discussed. The hearing focused on the legal actions taken against the former president.
summary: Former Justice Department special counsel Jack Smith defended two criminal indictments against President Trump on Capitol Hill. He defended the indictments on Capitol Hill.

title: Nepal disaster exposes global adaptation accountability gap
content:
A recent disaster in Nepal has exposed a significant gap between climate‑risk knowledge and the actions needed to protect communities. According to a report on Climate Home News, understanding of accelerating climate risks and how to adapt to them has grown over the past two decades, yet this knowledge has not been implemented quickly enough to safeguard affected populations.  

The post, titled “Ne pal’s disaster has laid bare the world’s adaptation accountability gap,” highlights that despite increased awareness, adaptation measures have lagged behind the pace of climate change, leaving communities vulnerable.
summary: Knowledge about accelerating climate risks and adaptation has grown over the past two decades, but it has not been put into practice fast enough to protect communities. The disaster in Nepal has laid bare the world’s adaptation accountability gap.
author: Climate Home News

title: UK banks provided $8.3bn in coal financing, topping Europe’s coal backers
content:
UK banks are Europe's largest financiers of the global coal industry, a new report finds.  

The study shows that UK‑based banks have supplied $8.3 billion ($6.2 billion) in coal financing over the past four years, since the 2021 COP26 summit in Glasgow where world leaders pledged to “phase down” coal use.  

Barclays and HSBC were identified as the leading banks behind the rise in coal funding.  

The report highlights the extent of UK banks’ involvement in coal financing.
summary: UK‑based banks have supplied $8.3bn (£6.2bn) in coal financing in the four years since COP26 in Glasgow 2021. The study says they are Europe’s biggest financial backers of the global coal industry, with Barclays and HSBC leading the rise.
author: Guardian Environment

title: New Study Shows Insects Provide Protection, Sanitation and Shelter to Vertebrates
content:
Insects play critical roles in ecosystems beyond serving as a food source, a new study published in Nature Reviews Biodiversity on Wednesday reveals. The research highlights that insects provide protection, sanitation, and shelter to vertebrates, underscoring their importance for conservation efforts.

The study describes insects as “little things that run the world,” noting that they support a wide range of vertebrate species—including birds, bats, reptiles, amphibians, and mammals—through these essential functions across diverse ecosystems.

By documenting the multifaceted contributions of insects to vertebrate well‑being, the research emphasizes the need to prioritize insect conservation in order to maintain healthy ecosystems.
summary: A new study published in Nature Reviews Biodiversity shows that insects provide protection, sanitation and shelter to vertebrates such as birds, bats, reptiles, amphibians and mammals. These functions highlight insects' importance beyond food, making them a priority for conservation efforts.
author: Guardian Environment

title: California Prepares for Kelvin Wave Expected to Reach San Francisco Bay by October
content:
California communities are preparing for the arrival of the so‑called “Kelvin wave,” a massive underwater band of warm water. The wave is moving toward southern California and is expected to reach the San Francisco Bay Area by early October as it continues toward Alaska.

Scientists warn that the wave could raise sea levels by a foot along the California coast. This increase would dramatically double the 8‑12‑inch rise in sea levels that has already been caused by climate change over the last century.
summary: Communities across California are preparing for the Kelvin wave, a massive warm‑water band that could raise sea levels by a foot along the coast. Scientists warn that the wave could double the 8-12in rise in sea levels already caused by climate change over the last century.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Wearable AI predicts prolonged sitting in women with chronic pelvic pain
content:
Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai have developed an artificial intelligence (AI) approach that uses data from wearable devices to forecast upcoming periods of prolonged sitting in women with chronic pelvic pain disorders.  

The AI system analyzes wearable‑device data to predict when these women are likely to experience extended sitting periods, offering a new tool for monitoring and potentially managing chronic pelvic pain.
summary: Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai developed an AI approach that uses data from wearable devices. The approach forecasts upcoming periods of prolonged sitting in women with chronic pelvic pain disorders.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Researchers develop model to study tumor microenvironment impact on IM-ADC therapy
content:
Researchers from Mass General Brigham and the University of Cyprus have developed a mathematical model to better understand how the tumor microenvironment affects the delivery and effectiveness of a new type of cancer therapy called an immunomodulatory antibody‑drug conjugate (IM‑ADC). The model aims to reveal strategies for modifying the tumor microenvironment to improve cancer therapy outcomes.  

The work, which focuses on the interaction between the tumor microenvironment and IM‑ADC delivery, is published in the Journal for ImmunoTherapy of Cancer.
summary: Researchers from Mass General Brigham and the University of Cyprus created a mathematical model to understand how the tumor microenvironment influences the delivery and effectiveness of an immunomodulatory antibody-drug conjugate (IM-ADC). The study was published in the Journal for ImmunoTherapy of Cancer.
author: Medical Xpress

title: CKDu primarily affects young men in heat-intensive agricultural work
content:
Kidney disease in Nicaragua has been linked to adolescents and young women, as well as individuals who do not work in heat‑intensive occupations. Chronic kidney disease of unknown origin (CKDu) is a global health concern that often progresses silently, without the classic metabolic symptoms of kidney disease such as obesity or diabetes. It is typically not diagnosed until it reaches an advanced stage, and it can be fatal.

While CKDu has traditionally been associated with young men engaged in heat‑intensive manual labor in equatorial agricultural communities, the recent findings in Nicaragua highlight a broader demographic at risk. The disease’s progression remains poorly understood, and it is often identified only after significant kidney damage has occurred.

CKDu continues to pose a serious public health challenge worldwide.
summary: CKDu is a global health concern that often progresses silently without classic metabolic symptoms such as obesity and diabetes. It is typically not diagnosed until advanced stages and primarily affects young men engaged in heat‑intensive manual labor in equatorial agricultural communities.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Omega Fatty Acids May Shut Down Cancer Defenses, Scientists Warn
content:
Omega‑3 fatty acids, long celebrated for their health benefits, have been called into question by recent scientific findings. The new research highlights a paradox: while these “healthy fats” support cardiovascular health, reduce systemic inflammation, and promote brain development and cognitive function, they may also interfere with cancer defenses and immunotherapy.

Scientists now warn that the compounds could have a previously unrecognized downside when it comes to cancer treatment. The findings suggest that the protective effects of omega‑3s may shut down certain immune responses that are critical for fighting cancer.
summary: Omega fatty acids are known for supporting cardiovascular health, reducing systemic inflammation, and promoting brain development and cognitive function. Scientists now warn that these compounds can shut down defenses against cancer and affect immunotherapy.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Personalized Support Boosts Genetic Testing Among Cancer Patients' Immediate Relatives
content:
A new study from researchers at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center found that first-degree relatives of cancer patients who received personalized support and navigation services were significantly more likely to undergo genetic testing. These relatives, defined as parents, siblings, and children, benefited from assistance throughout the testing process.

The research indicated that nearly half of the relatives who received this support carried a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation. These specific genetic markers are associated with a higher risk of developing cancer.
summary: First‑degree relatives of cancer patients who received personalized support and navigation services were significantly more likely to undergo genetic testing. The study, conducted by researchers at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, found that nearly half of those relatives carried a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: US Benzodiazepine Prescriptions Drop Sharply Over Past Decade, Study Finds
content:
Benzodiazepine prescriptions dropped sharply in the United States over the past decade, research finds.

Rutgers Health researchers reported that the number of prescriptions dispensed for benzodiazepines such as Xanax and Valium declined during the past 10 years. The decline may indicate that doctors have become more cautious about prescribing these sedatives.

The findings were presented by Rutgers Health researchers.
summary: Rutgers Health researchers found that prescriptions for benzodiazepines like Xanax and Valium declined in the United States over the past 10 years. The study suggests this drop indicates doctors have become more cautious about prescribing these sedatives.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Report Finds Gaps in Care for Australian Children with Familial Hypercholesterolemia
content:
A new report has revealed critical gaps in the care of Australian children with a preventable pediatric disorder that can lead to premature cardiovascular disease (CVD). The findings highlight that many children with the condition are not receiving the necessary monitoring and treatment.

Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a common genetic disorder that affects how the body processes low‑density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL‑C) from birth and significantly increases the risk of heart disease and early heart attacks in adulthood.
summary: A new report has revealed critical gaps in the care of Australian children with the preventable disorder familial hypercholesterolemia. Familial hypercholesterolemia is a common genetic disorder that disrupts LDL‑C processing from birth and raises the risk of heart disease and early heart attacks in adulthood.
author: Medical Xpress

title: People Switching from Wegovy Injections to Pill Continue Losing Weight, Study Finds
content:
A real‑world study found that patients who switched from Novo Nordisk’s obesity injections to the Wegovy pill continued to lose weight. The study’s data suggest that the weekly injection regimen may not be necessary for all patients.

According to the findings, patients can consider more convenient treatment options without sacrificing weight‑loss benefits. The Wegovy pill offers an alternative that may reduce the burden of daily injections.
summary: A real‑world study found that people who switched from Novo’s Wegovy injections to the Wegovy pill continued to lose weight. The data suggests patients may not need to take weekly injections forever and could opt for more convenient treatments.
author: CNBC Business

title: US food industry funds influencers to counter RFK Jr's Maha campaign
content:
A “freaked out” U.S. food industry is reportedly hitting back at the Maha movement by funding social‑media influencers, according to an investigation by the Guardian and Documented. The report notes that cross‑partisan support in Washington on issues such as pesticides and food additives is seen as a threat to the industry’s bottom line.

The investigation says some of the country’s largest food and agriculture corporations are paying influencers to counter elements of Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Make America Healthy Again platform. Kennedy, who has been appointed secretary of health and human services, argues that chronic illness in the U.S. is primarily caused by processed foods, dyes, exposure to certain chemicals, poor farming practices, and an overuse of what he claims are dangerous vaccines.

The Maha movement blends mainstream concerns about food and farm safety with conspiracy theories about medicine, milk, and other topics. A Maha “summit” in Washington this week will feature JD Vance and several members of Trump’s cabinet. The investigation was conducted by the Guardian and Documented.
summary: Some of the biggest food and agriculture corporations in the US are funding a campaign that pays social media influencers to combat elements of Robert F Kennedy Jr’s Make America Healthy Again platform, according to an investigation by the Guardian and Documented. The Maha movement, which blends mainstream concerns about food and farm safety with conspiracy theories, will hold a summit in Washington this week featuring JD Vance and several members of Trump’s cabinet.
author: Guardian Business

title: Engineered nanostructured surfaces could offer a new way to limit marine biofouling
content:
Researchers at Sultan Qaboos University have developed engineered surfaces that combine microscopic patterns with zinc oxide nanorods. The new surfaces are designed to reduce the attachment of bacteria and microalgae, organisms that contribute to biofouling on submerged marine and industrial equipment.

The combination of microscopic patterns and zinc oxide nanorods creates a surface that interferes with the initial stages of biofouling. By limiting bacterial and microalgal attachment, the engineered surfaces aim to mitigate the buildup that typically occurs on marine and industrial equipment.

The new surfaces could offer a new way to limit marine biofouling.
summary: Researchers at Sultan Qaboos University have developed engineered surfaces that combine microscopic patterns with zinc oxide nanorods to reduce the attachment of bacteria and microalgae—a process that contributes to biofouling on submerged marine and industrial…

title: Wild crabapples offer genetic resource for apple breeding
content:
A new study suggests that wild crabapples may help strengthen domestic apple varieties.  

The research, published in Horticulture Research, was conducted by Ben Mansfeld, an assistant professor of biology in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis.  

Mansfeld’s work offers apple breeders a genomic resource that could harness the genetic potential of humble crabapples.
summary: A new study published in Horticulture Research by Ben Mansfeld, an assistant professor of biology in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis, provides apple breeders with a genomic resource to help harness the power of humble crabapples. The research suggests that wild crabapples can strengthen apple varieties.
author: Phys.org

title: Kentucky entomologist develops gene‑silencing tech to target invasive beetles
content:
Gene‑silencing technology to protect forests from invasive pests

A forest entomologist at the University of Kentucky is advancing a pest‑control approach that targets destructive forest beetles while minimizing effects on surrounding wildlife. The method uses gene‑silencing technology to specifically disrupt beetle populations, offering a more selective alternative to conventional pesticides.
summary: A forest entomologist at the University of Kentucky is advancing a pest‑control approach that targets destructive forest beetles. The approach is designed to minimize effects on surrounding wildlife.
author: Phys.org

title: Who decides what time it is? The politics behind contested clocks
content:
University of Queensland researchers have found that there is no official global time‑zone system, a conclusion that comes amid ongoing local debates over time zones and seasonal shifts.  

The study highlights the lack of a worldwide standard for setting time, even as communities continue to argue over how best to align their clocks with daylight and regional needs.
summary: Despite contentious local debates about time zones and seasonal shifts, University of Queensland research shows there is no official global time zone system.
author: Phys.org

title: Jet diffusion wakes detected in quark‑gluon plasma after 20 years, matching 19.5° angle
content:
Scientists have reported the first detection of jet diffusion wakes in quark‑gluon plasmas, a milestone achieved after two decades of searching. The observation mirrors the diffusion wakes that form behind boats moving over smooth, deep water.

In water, a boat creates a pair of diffusion wakes that veer off at a theoretical angle of 19.5° from the line directly behind it, while turbulence remains along that central line. The newly identified plasma wakes exhibit a comparable angular pattern, confirming long‑standing theoretical predictions.
summary: Jet diffusion wakes have been detected in quark‑gluon plasmas after two decades of search. The wakes appear at a theoretical angle of 19.5° from the central line, the same angle predicted for diffusion waves behind boats on smooth water.
author: Phys.org

title: New simulations link first stars to cosmic fingerprints visible today
content:
Researchers from the University of Bath in the U.K., the University of Chicago in the U.S., and the Institut d'Astrophysique de Paris in France have utilized some of the most detailed simulations to date to investigate the formation of the first stars and galaxies. The MEGATRON project employs these advanced models to explore how these early celestial bodies illuminated the previously dark cosmos.

The simulations further examine how the first stars and galaxies enriched the universe with chemical elements. These elements are identified as the building blocks for everything in the surrounding universe.
summary: Researchers from the University of Bath, University of Chicago, and Institut d'Astrophysique de Paris used detailed simulations to investigate the formation of the first stars and galaxies. The MEGATRON project explores how these celestial bodies lit up the early universe and enriched it with chemical elements.
author: Phys.org

title: E. coli survives longer in poultry-amended Georgia onion soils, two-year study finds
content: New research indicates that poultry litter-based soil amendments and weather conditions, particularly extreme weather events, can influence the survival duration of bacteria in agricultural soils used for sweet onion production. The study specifically found that E. coli survives longer in Georgia onion soils amended with poultry litter. These findings may help inform food safety risk management strategies for produce growers.
summary: New research shows that poultry litter-based soil amendments and extreme weather events can influence how long bacteria survive in agricultural soils used to grow sweet onions. The findings could help inform food safety risk management for produce growers.
author: Phys.org

title: Study finds engagement timing and decision power shape trust in co-design
content:
A recent participant satisfaction study examines the effectiveness of co-design projects, which aim to include stakeholders as members of the design team. While these initiatives provide stakeholders with a seat at the table, few previous studies have evaluated whether participants actually feel heard.

The research indicates that meaningful participation is shaped by specific factors, including how and when individuals are engaged. Additionally, the study highlights that the distribution of decision-making power plays a crucial role in determining the quality of stakeholder involvement in these collaborative efforts.
summary: A participant satisfaction study evaluated whether stakeholders in co-design projects feel heard. The research found that meaningful participation is shaped by how and when people are engaged and who holds decision-making power.
author: Phys.org

title: El Niño: Pacific Ocean disturbance triggers global heat and extreme weather
content:
El Niño is a periodic disturbance in the Pacific Ocean that is amplified by atmospheric feedback mechanisms. This phenomenon occurs every few years and releases heat into the environment.

The event is known for unleashing extreme weather conditions around the globe.
summary: A disturbance in the Pacific Ocean is amplified by atmospheric feedback mechanisms every few years. This process unleashes heat and extreme weather around the globe.
author: New Scientist

title: MIT study: Lung cancer cells evade KRAS inhibitors via gene amplification or type switch
content: Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology have identified two distinct mechanisms by which lung cancer cells evade drugs designed to inhibit KRAS. According to the findings, some tumor cells develop resistance by amplifying the KRAS gene, while others undergo a change in their tumor type.
summary: MIT researchers discovered that some tumor cells develop resistance by amplifying the KRAS gene. Others change their tumor type.
author: MIT News

title: Orionid Meteor Shower Peaks in October as Earth Passes Halley's Comet Debris
content:
The Orionid meteor shower is set to peak in October, offering a brief window of activity for observers. This annual celestial event occurs as the Earth moves through a stream of debris left behind by Halley’s Comet.

During this period, the resulting meteors will streak across the night sky, marking the peak of the shower's visibility.
summary: The Orionid meteor shower peaks in October. Earth passes through debris left behind by Halley's Comet.
author: BBC Science

title: NRC Grants First U.S. Construction Permit for BWRX-300 Small Modular Reactor
content:

content:

content:

title: Apple to unveil HomePad smart hub with 6‑inch display on Oct. 13
content:
Apple is set to unveil its long‑rumored smart‑home hub, dubbed the HomePad, on October 13th. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that the device will be announced alongside a new HomePod mini and an upgraded Apple TV, with all three products slated to showcase Apple’s overhauled AI‑powered assistant, Siri.

The HomePad will be the centerpiece of the event. Gurman says it will feature a 6‑inch display that can be mounted on a wall or placed on a countertop. The hub is described as “about as thick as an iPhone” and will have bezels similar to older iPads.

The full story is available on The Verge.
summary: Apple will reveal its HomePad smart hub on Oct. 13 along with a new HomePod mini and an upgraded Apple TV. The hub will feature a 6‑inch display and showcase Siri AI, Apple's overhauled AI‑powered assistant.

title: Samsung unveils Galaxy SmartTag 3, smaller tracker with longer battery and iPhone support
content:
Samsung has unveiled its third‑generation Bluetooth tracker, the Galaxy SmartTag 3. The new device is smaller and offers longer battery life, and it introduces cross‑OS tracking features that allow users to share location data with friends and family across different platforms.

Leaks show the SmartTag 3 adopts a squircle shape similar to the original model but lacks a key‑ring cutout. Users who wish to attach the tracker to keys or a carabiner will need to purchase one of Samsung’s protective cases. The tracker also carries an IP67 rating, providing protection against dust and water.
summary: Samsung announced the third‑generation Galaxy SmartTag 3, a smaller Bluetooth tracker with improved battery life and cross‑OS support that lets users share tracking information with friends and family, including iPhone users. The device uses a squircle shape without a key‑ring cutout, requiring a protective case to attach to keys or a carabiner, and it has an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance.

title: Samsung revamps two-year-old Galaxy Tab S10 Plus with new S12 Plus model
content:
Samsung has announced the Galaxy Tab S12 Plus and Ultra, but no regular Tab S12 model will be released this year.  

Since the Galaxy Tab S10 line, Samsung has refreshed its flagship Ultra tablet annually while alternating between regular and Plus variants.  This year’s S12 series therefore includes an Ultra model that is largely unchanged from last year’s Tab S11 Ultra, and a Plus variant that offers a significant overhaul of the two‑year‑old Tab S10 Plus.  

Because there is no regular Tab S12, owners of the smaller size will have to wait until 2027 for the next version.  The Tab S12 Plus is positioned as a meaningful update for Tab S10 Plus or older owners, featuring a slightly larger and brighter 12.6‑inch display.
summary: Samsung introduced the Galaxy Tab S12 Plus, a significantly updated version of the two‑year‑old Tab S10 Plus. The S12 Plus has a slightly larger, brighter 12.6‑inch display and launches alongside a Tab S12 Ultra that has few changes from the Tab S11 Ultra, with no regular Tab S12 released.

content:

title: Tokyo court rules AI voice clone of actor Kenjiro Tsuda violated his publicity rights
content:
A Tokyo district court ruled on Wednesday that an AI tool which copied actor Kenjiro Tsuda’s “lustrous” baritone voice violated his rights, marking a landmark decision that extends publicity‑right protection to human voices.

The judgment concluded a legal action brought by Tsuda, best known for voicing the character Kento Nanami in the anime Jujutsu Kaisen, against a TikTok account that had used AI‑generated videos to clone his voice. The court held that the voice should enjoy the same legal protection afforded to other aspects of a person’s publicity rights.

The ruling establishes that a person’s vocal characteristics are protected under Japanese law, setting a precedent for future cases involving AI‑generated reproductions of individual voices.
summary: The Tokyo district court ruled that the human voice is protected under publicity rights in a case involving actor Kenjiro Tsuda. Tsuda won the lawsuit against a TikTok account that used an AI tool to clone his “lustrous” baritone voice in videos.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Lisa Nandy says under‑16 social media ban is only a staging post in safety drive
content:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said the United Kingdom’s online‑safety measures are only a “staging post,” warning technology firms that the government’s crackdown will continue. She added that the UK aims to be a “pioneer of tech as a force for good.”

Nandy referred to the government’s earlier announcement that teenagers under 16 would be barred from “high‑risk” social‑media apps, while platforms deemed safer would face additional restrictions. The statement signals that further regulatory steps are expected.

The culture secretary’s comments underscore the administration’s intent to expand its online‑safety agenda beyond the current age‑based ban.
summary: Culture secretary Lisa Nandy warned technology firms that the government's online safety crackdown is not finished and that the ban on under‑16s from social media platforms is only a “staging post”. Earlier this year the government announced that teenagers under 16 would be barred from “high‑risk” social media apps while safer platforms would face restrictions.

title: Bank of England governor calls for right to intervene in AI amid rogue model threats
content:
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that authorities must keep a “right to intervene” in the artificial‑intelligence sector as concerns mount that rogue AI models could threaten the financial system.  

Bailey said the rapid advancement of frontier AI models, several of which have gone rogue in recent months, presents “real and increasingly significant” risks and diminishes society’s ability to supervise and act when problems arise.  

He emphasized that without such intervention powers, the financial system could be held hostage by malfunctioning or malicious AI.
summary: Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey said authorities must retain the right to intervene in the AI industry. He warned that rogue frontier AI models pose real, increasingly significant risks that could threaten the financial system and reduce society’s ability to supervise and act when problems arise.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Rehabilitated green sea turtle Jurassic released into Atlantic with satellite tracker
content:
A 215‑pound adult male green sea turtle named Jurassic has been released back into the Atlantic Ocean after undergoing rehabilitation in Florida.  

The turtle was equipped with a satellite tracker at the time of release to monitor his movements.  

The release marks the completion of his rehabilitation program and initiates ongoing tracking of his post‑release behavior.
summary: Jurassic, a 215‑pound adult male green sea turtle, was released back into the Atlantic Ocean after rehabilitation in Florida. He was fitted with a satellite tracker to monitor his movements.

content: FlyDubai flight FZ1073, bound for Israel, made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after a violent incident in the cockpit. The emergency landing was carried out following the altercation, according to eyewitness accounts from those on board. No further details on injuries or the aircraft’s status were provided.

content:
Hurricane Polo struck parts of Mexico, producing flooding and widespread damage. Aerial footage captured streets inundated with water, while ground images revealed roofs that had been damaged and branches that had fallen.

The visual evidence also showed residents working to clear debris from the affected areas. The combined impact of the storm has left communities dealing with both water and structural damage.
summary: Hurricane Polo has caused flooding and damage in parts of Mexico. Aerial footage shows inundated streets and ground images show damaged roofs, fallen branches and residents clearing debris.

content:

Union leaders said the demonstration highlighted what they describe as a lack of government action on the issue, underscoring calls for increased resources for the fire service.

content:

content:

Andrew Smith of Queen Mary University of London said people have been “buying into the detoxification of the party,” despite its legacy as an anti‑Semitic and racist organization.

content:

content:

The last U.S. forces left an air base in northern Iraq under a deal between Baghdad and Washington, finalizing the agreed‑upon pullout.

title: Trump admin moves $175m of State human rights fund to rightwing causes
content:
Top Trump figures are moving to allocate more than $175 million of the State Department’s flagship human‑rights fund to a slate of right‑wing projects as the funding deadline approaches. The proposed awards include a $40 million anti‑communism grant, financing for a group that promotes white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign targeting Brazil’s supreme court, and programs that would reward European allies who defend “western civilisational norms.”  

Critics have highlighted 43 awards totaling $176.9 million that would bolster conservative causes worldwide and could provoke anger from U.S. allies over perceived interference in internal politics. According to The Guardian, the grants represent most of the $205 million Congress appropriated for the entire Human Rights and Democracy Fund (HRDF).
summary: The Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175 million of the State Department’s human rights and democracy fund to awards that include a $40 million anti‑communism grant, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court, and programs for ideological allies in Europe. content:

title: Global survey shows wide variation in bone metabolism biomarker testing
content:
Global survey reveals major variation in the measurement of bone and mineral metabolism biomarkers

Researchers from the International Osteoporosis Foundation (IOF) and the International Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (IFCC) Joint Committee on Bone Metabolism published a study on August 7, 2026, in Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine. The study examined self‑reported practices among laboratories that measure bone status indices (BSIs) in blood tests. It collected 231 responses from 41 countries.

The findings show substantial variation in global BSI laboratory practices, which limits data sharing, test standardization and clinical impact.
summary: Researchers from the International Osteoporosis Foundation and the International Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine Joint Committee on Bone Metabolism published a study on self‑reported practices of laboratories measuring bone status indices in blood tests. title: Micro-Athlete Mini-Heart Study Reveals Exercise Limits on Heart Health
content:
Can exercise do more harm than good? Mini-heart research is uncovering new answers

The phrase “Exercise is medicine” is widely cited, yet the idea that more exercise is always better is being questioned. Researchers are exploring what constitutes excessive exercise and how it can impact the heart. Questions remain about whether running a marathon or competing in an Ironman triathlon truly boosts health or could have the opposite effect.

To investigate these concerns, scientists have developed the Micro‑Athlete mini‑heart—a heart‑on‑a‑chip that mimics the human heart. This model is providing researchers with valuable new insights into cardiovascular disease and the effects of intense physical activity.

The mini‑heart research is uncovering new answers about the relationship between exercise intensity and heart health.
summary: Researchers are using the Micro-Athlete mini-heart, a heart-on-a-chip that mimics the human heart, to study how excessive exercise can harm the heart. The study aims to determine what counts as too much exercise and its impact on cardiovascular disease.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Multimorbidity identified in most Japanese home care patients
content:
Japan’s aging population is driving an increase in home‑based medical care, where physicians routinely visit older adults who have difficulty traveling to clinics or hospitals.  

Multimorbidity—having more than one chronic condition—has long been common among these home‑care patients. However, few studies have examined how widespread it is in this setting.  

The lack of data on multimorbidity prevalence highlights a gap in understanding the health needs of Japan’s growing home‑care population.
summary: Japan's aging population is resulting in more older adults receiving home-based medical care, where physicians regularly visit patients who have difficulty going to clinics or hospitals. Although multimorbidity has long been common among home care patients, few studies have assessed its prevalence in this population.

title: Daniek van Aarle's computer-generated ultrasound images rival real ones
content:
Simulated ultrasound images help develop better cardiovascular diagnostics

Daniek van Aarle, a Ph.D. candidate, has long challenged ultrasound researchers with the question, “Which of these two ultrasound images is real?” She presented this challenge at scientific conferences to highlight the realism of her work.

On September 29, van Aarle defended her doctoral research on computer‑generated, or virtual, ultrasound images. The study demonstrates that the synthetic images are almost indistinguishable from real ones. In her demonstration, one image was taken from a patient while the other was produced entirely by a computer.

The research suggests that virtual ultrasound imaging could improve cardiovascular diagnostic tools by providing realistic training and testing data.
summary: Daniek van Aarle defended her Ph.D. research on Sept. 29, showing that computer-generated ultrasound images can be almost indistinguishable from real ones. One image in her study came from a patient, while the other was entirely computer-generated.

title: Hidden habits that worsen social anxiety and how to break them
content: Social anxiety is more common than many think, according to a new piece titled “Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them.” The article aims to inform readers about the condition and identify everyday behaviors that can intensify anxiety in social settings. It also outlines steps individuals can take to interrupt those patterns and improve their comfort in social interactions.
summary: Social anxiety is more common than many think. The article discusses hidden habits that worsen it and ways to break them.

content:

title: Study finds diverse small-field crops improve bird habitats
content:
A new study published in the journal Landscape Ecology finds that planting a variety of crops in small field patches provides improved habitat for birds.  

The research highlights that diverse, fragmented agricultural landscapes support bird populations, which in turn help control pests and disperse seeds. By fostering richer bird communities, these mixed‑crop fields can also contribute to healthier soil and water quality.  

The findings suggest that small, heterogeneous fields may be a practical strategy for enhancing biodiversity and ecosystem services in agricultural regions.
summary: A new study published in Landscape Ecology shows that growing a variety of crops in small field patches creates better habitats for birds. Birds eat pests, disperse seeds and are considered indicators of a healthy environment.

title: University of Queensland software aims to improve AI analysis of plant microscopy images
content:

According to UQ Ph.D. student Tianqi Wei, even advanced vision‑language models struggle to interpret images of microscopic plant details, a challenge the new software seeks to overcome.

title: Thermal cameras and AI track bird collisions at offshore wind turbine in yearlong study
content:

The technology performed effectively under challenging conditions and produced rare real‑world data on bird movements around the turbine.
