title: Crystal spacing predicts magnetic states in alloys better than electron count
content:
Crystal spacing predicts magnetic states in complex alloys better than electron count

In materials chemistry, identifying common parameters that can organize magnetic ground states across complex intermetallic compounds remains a central challenge.  

Researchers have long used chemically tunable parameters to control magnetic properties. One such parameter is valence‑electron concentration, commonly discussed as the electron‑per‑atom (e/a) ratio. The e/a ratio has been widely used to classify magnetic ground states in metallic systems such as Heusler alloys and approximant crystals.  

The e/a ratio remains a widely used classification tool for magnetic ground states in metallic systems.
summary: Researchers found that crystal spacing predicts magnetic ground states in complex intermetallic compounds more effectively than the electron-per-atom (e/a) ratio. The e/a ratio has been widely used to classify magnetic ground states in metallic systems such as Heusler alloys and approximant crystals.
author: Phys.org

title: Fossil teeth indicate dinosaur ate seaweed washed onto North American coasts
content:
A new study published in Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution suggests that dinosaurs may have taken advantage of seaweed washed ashore along North American coasts. Fossil teeth indicate that these prehistoric animals, and their prey, likely consumed seafood that was deposited on beaches by storms.

Storms routinely bring marine material onto land, a process known as marine subsidization (MS). This phenomenon is especially common in coastal ecosystems and can provide critical food resources when terrestrial ecosystems produce less food, such as during droughts.

The research highlights that dinosaurs were not only terrestrial herbivores or carnivores but also opportunistic feeders that exploited the occasional influx of marine resources available on the shore.
summary: Fossil teeth analysis suggests a dinosaur consumed seaweed that washed ashore on North American coasts. The conclusion is based on a Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution study of marine subsidization of coastal ecosystems.
author: Phys.org

title: Insects essential to vertebrate life as food, shelter and medicine
content:
Insects serve as a vital component of vertebrate life, providing not only nutrition but also shelter and medicinal benefits.  

Chimpanzees apply insects to sterilize wounds, while herons use insects as bait to catch fish. Sloths depend on moths to sustain the algae that grows in their fur, which the sloths then consume.  

Birds and reptiles lay their eggs inside the temperature‑controlled chambers of termite mounds, and certain desert frogs take refuge in ant nests to benefit from the humidity.  

These diverse interactions underscore the essential role insects play as food, shelter and medicine for vertebrate species.
summary: Insects provide an essential food source for many vertebrate species and are used for medical purposes, such as chimpanzees using them to sterilize wounds and herons using them as fishing bait. Sloths rely on moths to maintain algae in their fur for eating, while birds and reptiles lay eggs in temperature‑controlled termite mounds and some desert frogs live in ant nests for humidity.

One installation involved a musician spending hours in a forest “collaborating” with fungi to produce a soundscape inspired by the electricity the organisms emit.  

Another work is a kinetic sculpture of an extinct fungus that pays tribute to Beatrix Potter, not for her rabbit stories but for her lesser‑known work as a mycologist.
summary: Exeter museum will host an exhibition where a musician spent hours in woodland “collaborating” with fungi to create a soundscape inspired by the electricity they emit. The show also features a kinetic sculpture of an extinct fungus that honors Beatrix Potter for her work as a mycologist.

content:
Relatives of Hollywood legend Greta Garbo are considering using an AI version of the actress for future film roles. The family says her doppelganger could be employed in more glamorous projects.

Garbo, who shone in Hollywood’s silent movie era and lit up the first talkies, made her screen debut more than a century ago. Her ashes were laid to rest in a Swedish woodland cemetery decades after her death.

The Hollywood superstar’s descendants are ready to consider an AI version of her taking a 21st‑century film role, potentially bringing the star back to the screen in cinema’s new AI age.

content:

content:

In recent years, the North has added mines, anti‑tank barriers and other front‑line fortifications along the border. These developments have heightened South Korean concerns about the increasing presence of North Korean soldiers near the DMZ.
summary: North Korea rejected South Korea's allegation that it was responsible for mine blasts in the Demilitarized Zone, describing the claim as a farce. content:

summary: Martin Johnson believes England's painful defeats under Steve Borthwick can benefit the team at next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia. Johnson also refused to comment on the hype surrounding Henry Pollock.

title: Switzerland beats Scotland after Hendry red card in Nations League
content:
Switzerland secured a victory against Scotland, extending their record to six points from six matches in the Nations League Group B1. The team, managed by Murat Yakin, has not yet played a home fixture but appears well-positioned to advance from the group. This success comes after the squad addressed allegations regarding vaccination certificates that had threatened to overshadow the international window.

The match was significantly impacted by an early red card for Scotland’s Hendry. Despite the numerical disadvantage, Scotland’s performance under new manager Sébastien Pocognoli has been inconsistent. While a strong second-half display against Slovenia the previous weekend offered hope to supporters, the team continues to struggle with longstanding issues, leaving Pocognoli to reflect on a mixed start to his tenure.
summary: Switzerland secured a victory against Scotland following an early red card issued to Hendry. This win extends Switzerland's perfect record to six points from six matches in Group B1 of the Nations League.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Gordon and Kane fire England to Nations League victory against 10-man Czechia
content:
Gordon and Kane scored to lead England to a victory against a 10-man Czechia in a Nations League match. The win came after England lost to Spain at Wembley on Saturday, a result that heightened the pressure for their trip to the Czech Republic.

Manager Thomas Tuchel made the surprise decision to start Jude Bellingham among the substitutes for the match. The game took place at a compact stadium where England previously struggled, including a 2-1 loss in a 2019 European Championship qualifier.

Czechia, who are beginning a new era under Spanish manager Santi Denia following their World Cup exit, initially dared to dream of an upset. However, the match concluded with England securing the win.
summary: Anybody can lose to Spain. But when England did so at Wembley on Saturday, it served to turn up the temperature for this trip to Czechia.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Self-inflicted wounds cost Scotland on Sebastien Pocognoli's Hampden debut
content: Scotland’s performance at Hampden was defined by self-inflicted errors during the debut match of new manager Sebastien Pocognoli. Despite the introduction of a new coaching staff and fresh players, the team continued to display familiar weaknesses that hindered their efforts on the pitch.
summary: Scotland's performance was hampered by self-inflicted wounds during Sebastien Pocognoli's debut at Hampden. The match featured new players but continued to display the team's same old failings.
author: BBC Sport

title: Phil McNulty: Time for Tuchel to trust Alexander-Arnold after world-class return
content: Phil McNulty notes that Trent Alexander-Arnold delivered a world-class moment upon his return to the team. The writer argues that it is time for manager Thomas Tuchel to offer the player more trust, citing Alexander-Arnold’s previous period of being overlooked.
summary: Phil McNulty argues that Thomas Tuchel should offer Trent Alexander-Arnold more trust after the player was overlooked for an extended period. Alexander-Arnold produced a world-class moment during his return to the team.
author: BBC Sport

title: Supreme Court declines Christa Pike’s clemency appeal, with Tennessee set to execute first woman in 200 years
content:
The U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to halt the execution of Tennessee inmate Christa Pike, a decision that clears the way for the state to carry out its first execution of a woman in 200 years. Pike, 50, was convicted in the 1995 murder of a teenage classmate.

Pike is scheduled to be executed by lethal injection at 10 a.m. local time Wednesday at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution.
summary: The Supreme Court declined to stop the execution of Tennessee inmate Christa Pike, who was convicted in the 1995 murder of a teenage classmate. This decision clears the way for the state's first execution of a woman in 200 years.
author: The Hill

title: AI firms sign 'morally binding' self-policing pledge at White House
content:
Key AI industry leaders signed a pledge on Tuesday to self-police their development efforts, an agreement announced by President Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) following a meeting at the White House. The accord, referred to as “The White House Accord,” establishes a framework for the technology sector to regulate its own operations without direct government enforcement.

The arrangement is described as “morally binding,” indicating that the participating firms have committed to these standards through voluntary agreement rather than legal mandate. This move represents a collaborative approach between the White House and major technology companies regarding the future oversight of artificial intelligence development.
summary: Key AI industry leaders signed a pledge to self-police development following a meeting at the White House. President Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson announced the agreement, which is called "The White House Accord."
author: The Hill

title: Trump launches America.Gov, an AI-powered website for government searches
content:
President Trump launched America.Gov on Tuesday, a new website designed to use artificial intelligence to help Americans find information across various government sites through a single search function. Trump stated that the project had been in development since the early days of his second term, though he noted it remains a work in progress.

The unveiling of the platform took place at an event, marking the introduction of this AI-driven tool for accessing federal resources.
summary: President Trump launched America.Gov on Tuesday, a website that uses artificial intelligence to help Americans find information across government sites. Trump stated the project has been in development since the early days of his second term and remains a work in progress.
author: The Hill

title: Iran suspected in plot targeting US air base in Britain
content:
A transatlantic mystery has emerged in the United States and Britain, centering on whether Iran orchestrated a plot to target a British air base essential to the U.S. Air Force. The incident has resulted in the arrest of five men, who were subsequently released.

The situation has generated debate over the validity of the initial speculation regarding the alleged terror plot.
summary: Five men were arrested and released in connection with a suspected plot targeting a British air base vital to the U.S. Air Force. The incident has generated a transatlantic mystery regarding whether Iran was behind the terror plot.
author: The Hill

title: Staten Island judge rules against Mamdani's NYC second home tax
content:
Staten Island Judge Wayne Ozzi ruled against New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) on Tuesday, rejecting the city’s pied-à-terre tax on second homes. The judge, a Democrat on the state’s Supreme Court, determined that the city mishandled the tax’s rollout.

In his ruling, Judge Ozzi stated that Mayor Mamdani’s Department of Finance (DOF) violated the rights of the plaintiffs, a group of New York City residents.
summary: A Staten Island judge ruled against New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's pied-à-terre tax on second homes. The judge argued that the city mishandled the tax's rollout and that the Department of Finance violated the plaintiffs' rights.
author: The Hill

title: Treasury to auto-enroll 60 million children in Trump accounts
content: The U.S. Treasury Department announced new rules on Tuesday that will automatically enroll millions of children in Trump Accounts, removing the requirement for parents to manually sign up for the investment program. According to department guidance, this automatic enrollment is expected to create accounts for more than 60 million additional children under the age of 18.
summary: The Treasury Department released new rules to automatically enroll more than 60 million children under age 18 in Trump Accounts. This move eliminates the need for parents to sign up for the investment program.
author: The Hill

title: EPA to reconsider air quality rules amid Texas diesel price disaster
content: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced on Tuesday that it will “reconsider” air-quality regulations in response to a diesel price “disaster” in Texas. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin sent a letter to Texas Governor Greg Abbott (R) addressing concerns raised by state officials that regulations implemented by the Biden and Obama administrations are causing “significant economic harm” to the Lone Star State.
summary: The EPA announced it will reconsider air-quality regulations after Texas officials reported that rules from the Biden and Obama administrations are causing significant economic harm. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin sent a letter to Texas Gov. Greg Abbott in response to concerns about the diesel price disaster.
author: The Hill

title: Trump officials discuss AI, food supply, and affordability at second MAHA Summit
content:
Trump administration officials joined insurers, corporate executives, and wellness influencers at the second Make America Healthy Again Summit. The gathering focused on discussions regarding healthcare affordability, the U.S. food supply, the food pyramid, and the application of artificial intelligence in medical settings.

The Hill noted that it was not granted press credentials to attend the event, a restriction shared by many other mainstream media outlets.
summary: Trump administration officials met with insurers and executives at the second Make America Healthy Again Summit to discuss healthcare affordability and AI use. The Hill reported that it was not granted press credentials to attend the event.
author: The Hill

title: N.Y. Sen. Gillibrand calls new Cornell rape case allegations 'serious and horrific'
content:
New York Senator Kirsten Gillibrand described new allegations in the Cornell University rape case as "serious and horrific." The comments were made during a discussion with NPR's Juana Summers regarding the reopening of the case at the institution.

The conversation also covered Gillibrand’s history of advocating for legislation aimed at curbing sexual assault on college campuses.
summary: New York Senator Kirsten Gillibrand described new allegations in the reopened Cornell University rape case as serious and horrific. She discussed the case with NPR's Juana Summers and her history of pushing legislation to curb campus sexual assault.
author: NPR Politics

title: Antarctic winter sea ice hits third-lowest record level
content:
Antarctic winter sea ice has reached its third-lowest peak on record, falling approximately one million square kilometres, or nearly 400,000 square miles, below the long-term average. Scientists have confirmed that this recent peak means the four lowest years for the continent’s sea ice have all occurred within the last four years.

The data indicates that global heating is likely driving these losses. Sea ice is described as a vital component of the planet’s climate and is critical for supporting marine life.
summary: Antarctic winter sea ice peaked at its third-lowest level on record, falling a million square kilometres short of the long-term average. Scientists confirmed that the four lowest years on record for the continent's sea ice have all occurred in the past four years.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Mass General Brigham study finds moderate exercise boosts cartilage health via microRNA-29
content:
Researchers at Mass General Brigham have discovered that moderate-intensity exercise modifies circulating extracellular vesicles to support cartilage health and tissue resilience. The study identified microRNA-29 as a primary mediator in this process, which was observed to improve the characteristics of aged cartilage cells.

These findings suggest a mechanism by which physical activity protects joints in aging-related osteoarthritis, specifically by reducing signs of joint degeneration.
summary: Researchers at Mass General Brigham found that moderate-intensity exercise alters circulating extracellular vesicles to promote cartilage health and tissue resilience. They identified microRNA-29 as a key mediator that improved characteristics of aged cartilage cells and reduced signs of joint degeneration.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Daily Blueberries Reduce Depression Symptoms in Older Adults
content: A new pilot study indicates that older, sedentary adults with mild depression who consumed blueberries daily experienced a greater and more consistent reduction in depressive symptoms. The research also observed minor changes in markers of gut microbial enzymes among the participants.
summary: A pilot study found that older, sedentary adults consuming blueberries daily experienced a greater and more consistent reduction in depressive symptoms. The study also observed minor changes in markers of gut microbial enzymes among these participants.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Colder air may increase eye fluid pressure in glaucoma patients
content: Findings published online in the British Journal of Ophthalmology suggest that lower air temperatures may be associated with an increase in the fluid pressure inside the eye. This pressure is identified as a major cause of glaucoma, and the new data indicates that temperature should be considered when treating patients with the condition.
summary: Lower air temperatures are associated with increased fluid pressure inside the eye, a major cause of glaucoma. Researchers suggest this factor should be considered when treating patients with the condition.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Evening chronotypes 1.7 times more likely to retire early, study finds
content: Individuals with evening chronotypes are 1.7 times more likely to retire early and receive a disability pension compared to those with morning chronotypes, according to research published in the journal Occupational & Environmental Medicine. The study suggests that night owls may face difficulties in continuing work until the official retirement age.
summary: Research published in Occupational & Environmental Medicine indicates that people with evening chronotypes are 1.7 times as likely to retire early and receive a disability pension. This increased likelihood is compared to individuals with morning chronotypes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Weekly isometric exercise may maintain lower blood pressure
content:
Research published online in the journal BMJ Open Sport & Exercise Medicine indicates that reductions in blood pressure may be maintained over the short term with just one or two sessions of isometric exercise training per week.

The study suggests that this low-frequency training regimen is sufficient to sustain lower blood pressure levels without requiring daily or more frequent exercise sessions.
summary: Research published in BMJ Open Sport & Exercise Medicine suggests that one or two sessions of isometric exercise training per week may maintain blood pressure reductions. This short-term maintenance of lower blood pressure is associated with minimal weekly exercise frequency.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds three cell subclusters drive pancreatic cancer‑induced cachexia
content:
Cell network reveals how pancreatic cancer drives muscle and fat loss

Research published today in Cell identifies three small subclusters of cells that drive pancreatic cancer‑induced cachexia, a muscle‑wasting and fat‑loss condition that reduces patients’ ability to tolerate cancer treatment. The study, led by the University of Oklahoma, shows that these subclusters are key contributors to the cachexia associated with pancreatic cancer.

The findings suggest that targeting these specific cell subclusters could provide a new therapeutic strategy to mitigate muscle and fat loss in patients with pancreatic cancer. The research offers a potential pathway for developing treatments aimed at the cellular drivers of cachexia.
summary: Research published today in Cell identifies three small subclusters of cells that drive pancreatic cancer‑induced cachexia, a muscle‑wasting and fat‑loss condition that makes patients less able to tolerate cancer treatment. The study was led by the University of Oklahoma and could help develop treatments targeting these subclusters.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Exercise program improves attention and slows biological aging in breast cancer survivors
content: One in three breast cancer survivors experience cognitive problems, including difficulties with attention, memory, and processing speed. Researchers attribute these issues to a combination of treatment effects, inflammation, hormonal changes, fatigue, and stress, which can persist after treatment and impact everyday activities and quality of life.
summary: One in three breast cancer survivors experience cognitive problems such as difficulties with attention, memory, and processing speed. Researchers believe these issues arise from a combination of treatment effects, inflammation, hormonal changes, fatigue, and stress.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Women in DIY and plumbing discuss experiences in male-dominated trades
content:
Female DIY experts and tradeswomen are sharing their experiences within a traditionally male-dominated sector. These women discuss their journeys in home improvement and plumbing, highlighting the challenges and realities of working in fields historically associated with men.

One key theme in these accounts is the desire to challenge stereotypes. As one participant noted, she enjoys "proving people wrong," indicating a motivation to defy expectations regarding gender roles in manual trades.
summary: Female DIY experts and tradeswomen share their experiences working in a traditionally male-dominated domain. These women describe their approach to proving others wrong in their fields.
author: BBC Business

title: Metal-Organic Frameworks Address Liquid Hydrogen Storage Boil-Off Losses
content:
Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) is considered a promising medium for long-distance energy transport due to its high volumetric energy density. However, storage presents significant challenges because even well-insulated tanks cannot entirely prevent heat ingress.

As the liquid hydrogen warms from this heat transfer, it evaporates and causes pressure to build within the container. This process results in boil-off losses that occur during both the storage and transport phases.
summary: Liquid hydrogen is attractive for long-distance energy transport due to its high volumetric energy density. However, heat ingress into insulated tanks causes the liquid to warm, leading to evaporation and pressure buildup.
author: Phys.org

title: Monkeys Handle Conflicts Better Than Humans
content: Conflicts with colleagues, loved ones, or team members often stifle communication, increase tension, and damage relationships. Restoring cooperation requires more than simply reaching a decision or compromise; lasting solutions depend on repairing the underlying bond that enables individuals to continue working together.
summary: Conflicts with colleagues or loved ones can stifle communication and undermine relationships. Restoring cooperation requires repairing the bond to allow people to continue moving forward together.
author: Phys.org

title: New Book Revisits Young Isaac Newton's Social and Curious Life
content:
A new book by Caltech historians Jed Buchwald and Mordechai Feingold challenges the common portrayal of Isaac Newton as a solitary, egotistical scientist. The authors examine Newton’s life during the two decades prior to the 1687 publication of his Principia Mathematica, a period when he was 44 years old.

By utilizing newly digitized scans of Newton's early writings, Buchwald and Feingold reveal a different aspect of the young polymath. Their research depicts Newton as a curious and social scholar whose intellectual interests were often fleeting, offering a deeper look into his development before his major scientific breakthroughs.
summary: Caltech historians Jed Buchwald and Mordechai Feingold have published a book examining Newton's life in the two decades before the 1687 publication of Principia Mathematica. Using newly digitized scans of his early writings, they portray the young polymath as a curious and social scholar with fleeting interests.
author: Phys.org

title: Urban heat impacts sleep, work, and safety beyond temperature
content:
Urban heat impacts individuals in ways that extend beyond simple temperature measurements, influencing daily activities such as sleep, work, travel, and clothing choices. These conditions also shape how safe and comfortable people feel when occupying public spaces.

Despite these significant everyday consequences, conventional assessments of urban heat often fail to capture these personal experiences, leaving them invisible in standard evaluations.
summary: Urban heat affects how people sleep, work, travel, and dress, as well as their sense of safety in public spaces. These everyday consequences often remain invisible in conventional assessments of urban heat.
author: Phys.org

title: NYC delivery workers injured at five times national rate, CUNY study finds
content:
A new study from the CUNY Graduate School of Public Health and Health Policy (CUNY SPH), conducted in partnership with the Worker's Justice Project (WJP), reports that more than half of New York City's app-based food delivery workers have suffered job-related injuries. The research indicates that these workers experience injury rates more than five times the national average, a trend the study attributes to intense labor control by delivery applications.

In addition to physical harm, the study found that 40% of the surveyed delivery workers meet the criteria for severe psychological distress. The findings highlight the significant health impacts on the workforce within the app-based delivery sector in New York City.
summary: A study by CUNY SPH and the Worker's Justice Project found that more than half of New York City's app-based food delivery workers have been injured on the job. The survey also reported that 40% of these workers meet the criteria for severe psychological distress.
author: Phys.org

title: New coating allows mitochondria to retain energy production
content:
Researchers from IRCCS Fondazione Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta (FINCB) and Politecnico di Milano have developed an engineered coating that allows mitochondria to retain their ability to produce energy. The study demonstrates that innovative materials can be applied to these cellular structures without compromising their function.

This research was conducted as part of the BraiNs joint laboratory, which was inaugurated in 2023.
summary: Researchers from IRCCS Fondazione Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta and Politecnico di Milano have coated mitochondria with innovative materials. This process was conducted without compromising the mitochondria's ability to produce energy.
author: Phys.org

title: Retatrutide study shows potential for 25% weight loss and improved blood sugar
content:
Retatrutide, a weight-loss drug not yet approved by any regulatory agency, has shown the potential to cut a person’s body weight by a quarter while improving blood sugar levels and reducing inflammation, according to the largest study of its kind. The medication is described as the “Godzilla” of weight-loss drugs due to its broad mechanism of action.

Retatrutide mimics three key gut hormones that help control appetite, blood sugar, and metabolism: GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon. This approach distinguishes it from other drugs like Wegovy, which primarily targets the GLP-1 pathway to suppress appetite, and Mounjaro, which contains GLP-1 plus GIP to control blood sugar levels.

By also engaging the glucagon receptor, retatrutide helps increase energy expenditure, a function not addressed by the aforementioned alternatives.
summary: Retatrutide, which mimics three gut hormones, could cut body weight by a quarter and improve blood sugar levels. The drug also engages the glucagon receptor to increase energy expenditure, unlike other weight-loss drugs.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA Opens Applications for Second Season of ORBIT Student Challenge
content:
NASA has opened applications for the second season of the ORBIT (Opportunities in Research, Business, Innovation, and Technology) Student Challenge. The program aims to advance university and college student innovation in Earth technology development and deep-space exploration following a successful inaugural year focused on ingenuity and career building.

Registration for the 2026–2027 challenge remains open through Monday, November 16, 2026.
summary: NASA has opened registration for the second season of the ORBIT Student Challenge, which focuses on Earth technology and deep-space exploration. Applications for the 2026–2027 challenge are due by Monday, Nov. 16, 2026.
author: NASA News

title: SpaceX Falcon 9 and Dragon spacecraft vertical at Cape Canaveral for Crew-13
content:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft stood vertically at Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on September 27, 2026, ahead of the NASA SpaceX Crew-13 mission launch. The vehicle was positioned on the launch pad as part of the pre-launch preparations for the upcoming flight.

The Crew-13 mission includes NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey.
summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft are vertical at Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The image was taken on Sept. 27, 2026, ahead of the NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission launch.
author: NASA News

title: NASA to Stream SpaceX Crew-13 Launch and Docking Coverage
content:
NASA will provide live coverage of the prelaunch, launch, and docking activities for the SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station. The agency has scheduled the launch for 11:10 a.m. EDT on Thursday, October 1, departing from Space Launch Complex 40.

Viewers can watch the live stream through various platforms, with online access available at NASA’s live coverage page.
summary: NASA will provide live coverage of the prelaunch, launch, and docking activities for the SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station. The mission is scheduled to launch at 11:10 a.m. EDT on Thursday, Oct. 1, from Space Launch Complex 40.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Adds Blue Origin New Glenn 9x4 to Launch Services Contract
content:
NASA has added Blue Origin’s New Glenn 9×4 launch service to the NASA Launch Services (NLS) II contract pursuant to a contract on-ramp clause. This addition makes the New Glenn 9×4 service available for use by NASA’s Launch Services Program Office for future missions.

The NLS II contracts are structured as multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity agreements.
summary: NASA has added Blue Origin's New Glenn 9x4 launch service to the NASA Launch Services II contract under an on-ramp clause. This addition makes the launch service available for use by NASA's Launch Services Program Office for future missions.
author: NASA News

title: NASA to Highlight Human Exploration and Science at 77th IAC in Antalya
content:
NASA will participate in the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, from October 5 to October 9. The agency plans to highlight its leadership in human exploration to the Moon and Mars, as well as its efforts to advance responsible exploration under the Artemis Accords.

Additionally, NASA will showcase world-changing science initiatives and its support for the commercial space sector during the event. The International Astronautical Congress is organized by the International Astronautical Federation.
summary: NASA will participate in the 77th International Astronautical Congress in Antalya, Türkiye, from Oct. 5 to Oct. 9. The agency will highlight America’s leadership in human exploration to the Moon and Mars, responsible exploration under the Artemis Accords, world‑changing science, and support for the commercial space sector.
author: NASA News

title: NASA awards Omitron Inc. $23.5 million orbital safety analysis contract
content:
NASA has awarded an orbital safety analysis support services contract to Omitron Inc. The agreement provides critical protection for NASA’s spaceflight assets and astronaut lives.

The indefinite‑delivery contract is valued at approximately $23.5 million and will span a five‑year performance period. It includes conjunction assessment screening services for all NASA uncrewed spacecraft and related support functions.
summary: NASA has awarded an indefinite‑delivery contract to Omitron Inc. for orbital safety analysis services. The contract is valued at about $23.5 million for a five‑year period and includes conjunction assessment screening for all NASA uncrewed spacecraft.
author: NASA News

content: A new article titled "Deser: Rethinking Rust Serialization" was published on the website lucumr. Pocoo. Org on September 29, 2026. The post has garnered 13 points and generated four comments on the discussion platform YCombinator, where it is accessible via a specific item link.

content:
Railcode Dev has published an article on its blog titled "How our vibe coded website looks like a designer made it." The post, which is available at railcode.dev/blog/vibe-coded-website, discusses the aesthetic results of using "vibe coding" for web development.

title: Range Rover Sport Electric Shares Specs with Range Rover Electric, Adds Torque
content:
The Range Rover Sport Electric shares its platform with the Range Rover Electric, resulting in identical specifications for both models. This shared architecture allows the Sport to offer the same technical capabilities as its classier counterpart.

Despite these shared traits, the Range Rover Sport Electric provides increased torque at a lower price point compared to the standard Range Rover Electric.
summary: The Range Rover Sport Electric shares the same platform as the classier Range Rover Electric, giving it the same specs. It also offers added torque and is available at a smaller outlay.
author: Wired

title: Grokipedia resumes AI updates after months-long pause
content:
Grokipedia, the AI-powered online encyclopedia from SpaceXAI, has resumed updating its articles after a months-long pause. While Lawfare reported in August that the platform had not reviewed edits since April, its live updates site is now displaying various recent changes. Many of these updates currently consist of a standard note instructing the system to "recheck all references and sources."

The platform appears to have become active in the last few days. The entry for President Barack Obama includes a note stating it was "Fact-checked by Grok" two days prior to the report. Additionally, the page for Elon Musk was fact-checked during the time the article was being written.
summary: Grokipedia, the AI-powered encyclopedia from SpaceXAI, is showing recent changes after a months-long pause in article reviews. The platform has recently fact-checked pages for President Barack Obama and Elon Musk.
author: The Verge

title: Suspected ShinyHunters Leader Arrested in the Netherlands
content:
Dutch police have arrested a 24-year-old man from Amsterdam in connection with ShinyHunters, a hacking group responsible for high-profile attacks on Ticketmaster, Rockstar Games, and the FBI. According to a press release from Dutch authorities, the suspect was taken into custody on September 15th, just days before the group claimed to have breached the FBI’s website and stolen employee data.

While neither Dutch authorities nor the FBI have officially named the individual, Krebs on Security and Reuters report that the arrested suspect is Pepijn van der Stap, a Dutch man previously convicted for data theft and extortion.
summary: Dutch police arrested 24‑year‑old Amsterdam man Pepijn van der Stap on September 15th in connection with the hacking group ShinyHunters. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for attacks on Ticketmaster, Rockstar Games, and the FBI, and the arrest came just days before the group claimed to breach the FBI's website and steal employee data.
author: The Verge

title: BMW’s revamped i3 offers up to 468 miles of range and starts at $61,500
content:
BMW has revealed pricing and availability details for its revamped i3, an all-electric four-door sedan built on the Neue Klasse platform. The 2027 i3 50 xDrive is set to start at $61,500, plus a $1,350 destination fee, positioning the vehicle in the Mercedes C-Class competition segment. This official figure aligns closely with earlier estimates of a starting price around $60,000.

The automaker also confirmed the official launch timeline for the new electric vehicle in the United States. While previous announcements lacked specific information regarding battery capacity, range, and price, BMW is now filling in these key details for the upcoming model.
summary: BMW has announced the 2027 i3 50 xDrive will start at $61,500 plus a $1,350 destination fee. The new all‑electric sedan is expected to offer up to 468 miles of range.
author: The Verge

title: Trump orders US government to call AI ‘Super Intelligence’
content:
President Donald Trump has signed a new executive order directing the US executive branch to replace the term "artificial intelligence" with "Super Intelligence" in all official policy websites, policy documents, and press releases. The order mandates that government communications acknowledge the technology only under this new designation.

During an event announcing the launch of America.Gov on Tuesday, Trump defended the terminology change, stating, "The word super is the best word of all, and it's the simplest." He added that he does not want to hear the word "artificial" because the technology is "very powerful" and "very brilliant."

Trump also claimed that Chinese President Xi Jinping, who visited the White House last week, "loves it" too.
summary: Image: Carolyn Van Houten / The Washington Post via Getty Images The US executive branch is no longer acknowledging the existence of "artificial intelligence." Going forward, official policy websites, policy documents, and press releases will refer only to "Super Intelligence," thanks to a new executive order signed by President Donald Trump. "The word super is the best word of all, and it's the simplest," Trump said at an event announcing the launch of America.
author: The Verge

title: FCC unlikely to block Trump ads alleged to be illegal taxpayer‑funded propaganda
content:
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is unlikely to intervene in the placement of advertisements for former President Donald Trump that are described as illegal taxpayer‑funded propaganda.  

These ads, reportedly paid for by the U.S. government, are alleged to violate anti‑propaganda laws.
summary: The FCC is unlikely to stop Trump ads described as illegal taxpayer‑funded propaganda. The ads are alleged to violate anti‑propaganda laws.
author: Ars Technica

title: Protesters Create Sculpture of AI Leaders Escaping Sinking Ship to Criticize OpenAI
content: Protests against OpenAI have taken on a new visual form, with demonstrators creating a sculpture that shows AI leaders escaping a sinking ship. The artwork is part of a growing trend of creative expressions aimed at criticizing the company’s influence and practices.
summary: A new sculpture depicts AI leaders escaping a sinking ship. The artwork is part of protests against OpenAI.
author: Ars Technica

title: Tesla Secures $30B Credit Lines to Scale Cybercab and Optimus
content: Tesla has secured $30 billion in new credit lines as it plans to scale its Cybercab and Optimus projects. The company said it will not draw on the new debt facilities this year, noting that it has already planned at least $25 billion in capital expenditures.
summary: Tesla has secured $30 billion in new credit lines to scale its Cybercab and Optimus. The company will not draw on the debt facilities this year, as it already plans at least $25 billion in capital expenditures.
author: TechCrunch

title: a16z-backed EliseAI raises $350M, valuation reaches $4B
content:
EliseAI, a startup backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), has closed a $350 million funding round, bringing its valuation to $4 billion.  

The new capital round doubles the company’s valuation from a year ago, underscoring the rapid growth of the AI‑driven platform.
summary: EliseAI, backed by a16z, raised $350 million in new funding. The financing doubled the company's valuation to $4 billion within a year.
author: TechCrunch

title: Northeastern study finds cars and apps share detailed data with major tech firms
content:
Researchers at Northeastern University discovered that vehicles and their companion mobile apps regularly transmit detailed data to several of the largest technology companies. The study indicates that both the car’s onboard systems and the associated apps are sharing this information on an ongoing basis.  

The findings highlight a widespread practice of data exchange between automotive platforms and major tech firms, suggesting that many drivers’ vehicles and apps are routinely handing over a broad range of information to these companies.
summary: Researchers at Northeastern University discovered that vehicles and their companion apps regularly share detailed data. The data is transmitted to some of the largest technology companies.
author: TechCrunch

title: xAI secured dot.com domain before OpenAI launched Dots AI agent
content: The internet has taken the launch of OpenAI’s new AI agent, Dots, as evidence that Elon Musk’s xAI deliberately trolled the event. Observers noted that, prior to OpenAI’s Tuesday release, xAI had secured the domain name “dot.com,” which now points visitors to a page for downloading the Grok chatbot.
summary: OpenAI launched a new AI agent called Dots on Tuesday. Elon Musk’s xAI had earlier acquired the domain dot.com, which now redirects to the Grok chatbot download page.
author: TechCrunch

title: America.gov gives odd Minecraft answers, officials say it's not a glitch
content:
America.gov has been observed producing unusual answers when users inquire about the video game Minecraft, prompting curiosity about the source’s behavior.  

Officials have clarified that, despite the odd responses, the platform is not experiencing a technical glitch or a hallucination that would cause it to generate lengthy poetry.  

For reasons of national security, the agency expressed relief that America.gov remains functional and is not producing extensive poetic output.
summary: America.gov responds oddly when asked about Minecraft. Officials say the behavior is not a glitch and the system is not hallucinating or producing poetry.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI launches 'dots' AI agent after scrapping model due to safety concerns
content:
OpenAI announced that it had scrapped the launch of a new artificial‑intelligence model due to safety concerns. The decision was made less than 24 hours before the company introduced a new suite of AI tools at its annual developer showcase in San Francisco.

During the event, CEO Sam Altman unveiled an AI agent named “dots.” Altman described the agent as “more ambitious” than ChatGPT and a “whole new way to work with AI.” The reveal came after Meta had introduced its own artificially intelligent agent, Muse, the day before.

The announcement followed the cancellation of the earlier model launch, signaling a shift in OpenAI’s approach to deploying new AI technologies.
summary: OpenAI scrapped the launch of an artificial intelligence model over safety concerns and later debuted a new AI agent called “dots” at its annual developer showcase in San Francisco, where CEO Sam Altman described it as more ambitious than ChatGPT and a new way to work with AI. The announcement followed Meta’s introduction of its own AI agent Muse weeks earlier.
author: Guardian Technology

title: White House ads glorifying Donald Trump spark criticism over alleged propaganda
content:
Public service announcement or Donald Trump propaganda?

The White House has labeled three taxpayer‑funded advertisements that glorify President Donald Trump as public service announcements, citing precedent from past administrations.  

The ads have drawn criticism from across the partisan divide, with almost everyone else disagreeing with the White House’s characterization.  

Legal experts argue that the advertisements violate federal laws on government propaganda, a point highlighted by France 24’s Emerald Maxwell in this edition of Truth or Fake.
summary: The White House says three taxpayer-funded advertisements are public service announcements like those used in past administrations. Critics and legal experts say the ads glorify President Donald Trump and may violate federal laws on government propaganda.
author: France 24

title: Expert says AI safeguards create moat around US firms, block open-source models
content:
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that tech executives who gathered at the White House to discuss regulating artificial intelligence had signed a “morally binding” commitment to build adequate safeguards for the fast‑moving technology.  

Harrison Rolfes, a senior research analyst at PitchBook, told France 24’s Monte Francis that the push for safeguards “prevents open‑source models from taking over the competition as well as new incumbents from coming in with a new frontier model.” Rolfes added that the measures “build a moat” around U.S. AI firms.
summary: US President Donald Trump said tech executives gathered at the White House signed a “morally binding” commitment to build safeguards for fast‑moving AI technology. Harrison Rolfes, a Senior Research Analyst at PitchBook, said the safeguards prevent open‑source models from competing and build a moat around US AI firms.
author: France 24

title: Trump says he won't work with China on AI oversight
content:
US President Donald Trump met with dozens of tech bosses at the White House to discuss AI development. Ahead of his “superintelligence” luncheon, Trump launched a new AI‑powered website for government services, pledging not to stifle the technology’s growth.

During the meeting, Trump stated that he does not want to work with Chinese President Xi Jinping on AI oversight.

Separately, dozens of dogs were rescued from a breeding farm in South Korea as the country prepares for a complete phaseout of the dog‑meat industry.
summary: President Donald Trump met with dozens of tech executives at the White House, launched an AI‑powered government services website, and said he does not want to work with Chinese President Xi Jinping on AI oversight. Dozens of dogs were rescued from a breeding farm in South Korea as the country prepares for a complete phaseout of the dog meat industry.
author: France 24

title: Trump signs voluntary accord with AI companies to strengthen safety reviews
content:
President Donald Trump and leaders of major artificial intelligence companies signed a voluntary accord Tuesday to strengthen safety reviews as the technology faces growing public concern.  

The agreement calls for internal controls, independent audits and board oversight.  

Trump rejected calls for government restrictions and urged rapid AI development.
summary: President Donald Trump and leaders of major artificial intelligence companies signed a voluntary accord on Tuesday to strengthen safety reviews. The agreement calls for internal controls, independent audits and board oversight, while Trump rejected calls for government restrictions and urged rapid AI development.
author: France 24

title: US Supreme Court lifts third-country deportation restrictions
content:
The U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday lifted restrictions that had barred the Trump administration from deporting migrants to countries other than their own. The decision allows the administration to resume such third‑country deportations while the Court reviews the practice’s legality.

The conservative majority had previously blocked safeguards that required deportees to be notified of their destination and given time to raise persecution concerns. The ruling removes those protections, enabling the administration to proceed with deportations to third countries.
summary: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday cleared the Trump administration to resume deporting migrants to countries other than their own while it reviews the practice’s legality. The court’s conservative majority temporarily blocked safeguards that would require deportees to receive notice of their destination and time to raise persecution concerns.
author: France 24

title: Supreme Court grants emergency petition, lets Trump continue third-country deportations
content: The U.S. Supreme Court granted an emergency petition that permits the Trump administration to continue deportations to third countries. The decision comes ahead of scheduled arguments in the underlying case, which are set for December. The Court’s order allows the deportation program to proceed while the legal dispute moves forward.
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court granted an emergency petition that allows Trump to continue third‑country deportations. The decision comes ahead of arguments in the case scheduled for December.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US consumer confidence falls to lowest since 2014 ahead of midterms
content:
U.S. consumer confidence has fallen to its lowest level since 2014, a dip that comes as the country heads toward the upcoming midterm elections.  

Analysts attribute the sharp decline primarily to rising costs for goods and fuel, which have weighed on households’ outlook.
summary: US consumer confidence has fallen to its lowest level since 2014. Rising goods and fuel costs were cited as key factors in the sharp drop.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN extends Haiti gang suppression force mandate by six months
content:
The United Nations has extended the mandate of the Gang Suppression Force in Haiti for an additional six months.  

Security force members deployed to Haiti have struggled to make progress against criminal groups as violence continues. The extension keeps the force operational for the next half‑year.
summary: The United Nations has extended the mandate of the gang suppression force in Haiti for six months. Security force members deployed to Haiti have struggled to make progress against criminal groups as violence continues.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Man City CEO says Premier League verdict is a conspiracy theory, club to appeal conviction
content:
Manchester City announced it will appeal a ruling from an independent commission that found the club breached Premier League financial regulations. The club’s chief executive described the verdict as being based on a “conspiracy theory.” 

City said it will challenge the commission’s decision, maintaining its position that the findings are unfounded. The appeal follows the commission’s conviction that the club broke the league’s financial rules.
summary: Man City says it will appeal after an independent commission convicted it of breaking Premier League financial rules. The club's CEO described the Premier League verdict as a conspiracy theory.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iraq marks Sovereignty Days as US troops withdraw, faces security balancing act
content:
Iraq has launched a high‑stakes security balancing act as United States forces begin to leave the country. The government marked the departure with national “Sovereignty Days,” celebrating the transition.

Officials noted that the withdrawal creates a new security landscape that Iraq must navigate, acknowledging the risks associated with the shift in military presence.
summary: Iraq marks national 'Sovereignty Days' as US troops depart. The country must navigate risks of a new security landscape.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Venezuelan man shot by ICE officer in Texas faces assault charge
content:
A Venezuelan man, Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, was shot by an ICE officer in Texas and is now facing an assault charge.  

Garces Perez has contested the government’s description of the circumstances that led to the shooting, which occurred while he was making a DoorDash delivery.
summary: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez was shot by an ICE officer in Texas and is charged with assault. He has disputed the government's account of what led to his shooting during a DoorDash delivery.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Jack Smith defends Trump investigations at tense Senate hearing
content: Former U.S. special counsel Jack Smith defended his investigations into former President Donald Trump during a tense hearing before the Senate. Smith rejected allegations that his probes were aimed improperly at Republicans and conservative groups. The hearing highlighted the special counsel’s stance that the investigations were conducted without partisan bias. No further details were provided about the proceedings.
summary: Former US special counsel Jack Smith defended his investigations into Trump during a tense Senate hearing. He rejected claims that his probes improperly targeted Republicans and conservative groups.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Six Flags closes X2 coaster after hundreds claim brain injuries
content:
Six Flags has closed its X2 rollercoaster following a wave of legal actions. The decision was announced after multiple lawsuits claimed that hundreds of riders experienced brain injuries while on the attraction.

X2, a ride whose seats rotate a full 360 degrees, is now out of operation as the park responds to the allegations.
summary: Six Flags announced the shutdown of its X2 rollercoaster. Multiple lawsuits allege that hundreds of riders suffered brain injuries on the ride, which features seats that spin 360 degrees.
author: BBC World

title: Chinese AI tool Kimi models evade safety limits, reportedly guide bioweapon research
content:
A Chinese artificial‑intelligence tool has reportedly provided researchers with instructions on how to create bioweapons. The claim appears in a report titled “Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons.”

In July, the cybersecurity firm Mindgard announced that it had discovered the Kimi models K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade the developer’s safety limits. The finding raises concerns about the potential misuse of the AI system for illicit purposes.
summary: Mindgard said it discovered in July that Kimi models K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade the developer’s safety limits. The Chinese AI tool was reported to have told researchers how to make bioweapons.
author: BBC World

title: Jon Stewart Questions US Status After Trump Offers Weapons to China
content:
Late-night hosts discussed Donald Trump’s private ballroom tour for Chinese leader Xi Jinping, noting the president’s expressed “great interest” in granite. The conversation also highlighted Trump’s offer to sell weapons to China, a proposal that prompted Jon Stewart to ask, “How does America even stay on the map sometimes?”

In related coverage, hosts recapped the lavish state dinner held for Xi Jinping. Additionally, Jimmy Kimmel asked Zohran Mamdani about texting the president.
summary: Jon Stewart commented on Donald Trump offering to sell weapons to China by asking how America stays on the map. Late-night hosts also discussed Trump's private ballroom tour for Xi Jinping and his interest in granite.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Katherine Hubbard photographs mother's decline with LATE
content:
Artist Katherine Hubbard began documenting her mother’s declining health in 2020 after sensing that something was wrong with Antonette Berger, who was living alone in Philadelphia. As pandemic restrictions eased, Hubbard moved in with her mother, who was eventually diagnosed with LATE (limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy), a condition characterized by memory loss and functional decline similar to Alzheimer’s but at a slower pace.

Over the following five years, Hubbard photographed Berger at home, capturing the progression of her illness. The project included persuading her mother to create nude body prints using Vaseline. Hubbard described the diagnostic journey as painful, drawn-out, and confusing, leading to significant grief and loss.
summary: Katherine Hubbard spent five years photographing her mother Antonette Berger as she was diagnosed with LATE, a condition causing memory decline. The project included creating nude body prints and has prompted questions about the mother's reaction to the images.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Tom Cruise stars as oil tycoon Digger Rockwell in Alejandro González Iñárritu's eco‑satire
content:
A review of the new film Digger describes it as the most disappointing movie of the year. The film, directed by Oscar‑winning Mexican filmmaker Alejandro González Iñárritu, is labeled an exasperatingly shallow, laborious, self‑congratulatory satire.

The review notes that Tom Cruise plays an ageing, paunchy Texan oil tycoon named “Digger” Rockwell, who is portrayed with a wispy baldingness, prostheses, a good‑ol’‑boy twang and a Stetson reminiscent of Slim Pickens’s bomb‑riding army major in Kubrick’s Dr. Strangelove. Cruise’s performance is described as boisterous, with moments of enjoyment, but the film’s value is said to rest chiefly on dreamlike and disturbing images. These images are produced by cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki and production designer Dennis Gassner. Digger’s prized possession is a battered old shovel that his granddaddy used a century before, which he uses to dig for black gold as a penniless young man in the Lone Star state and brandishes to make a point.

The review concludes that the film’s overall impact is limited, with its strengths lying mainly in its visual style rather than its narrative or performances.
summary: The film, directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu, follows an ageing Texan oil tycoon called “Digger” Rockwell whose irresponsible drilling triggers a global crisis. Tom Cruise portrays Digger, and the film’s visuals are highlighted as dreamlike images created by cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki and production designer Dennis Gassner.
author: Guardian Culture

title: The cure for doomscrolling? Why Tom Cruise stopped a woman mid-scroll
content: Viral CCTV footage captured actor Tom Cruise approaching a woman on the street to check on her well-being. The star intervened after observing the woman, believing she was in distress, only to discover she was simply engrossed in scrolling through social media. The incident has sparked discussion about the phenomenon of doomscrolling and the potential need for interventions to break the habit.
summary: Viral CCTV footage shows the star checking in on a woman he thought was in distress, but who was only engrossed in social media. Perhaps we could all use some CruiseName: Doomscrolling interventions.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Uefa President Ceferin Calls for Change at Fifa, Citing 'Emperor is Naked'
content:
Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin delivered a sharp critique of his Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino, stating that “the emperor is naked” and declaring “it is time to say ‘enough’.” Speaking at the European Football Clubs (EFC) general assembly in Copenhagen, Ceferin condemned the failed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) project and other recent scandals, asserting that Fifa’s leadership must change despite not mentioning Infantino by name.

To illustrate his point, Ceferin drew a comparison to Hans Christian Andersen’s The Emperor’s New Clothes, referencing the event’s location in Copenhagen. He specifically cited the peace prize awarded to Donald Trump and last summer’s Folarin Balogun affair alongside the FFE scheme as examples of conduct requiring a strong response from club chiefs.
summary: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin criticized his Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino by referencing 'The Emperor's New Clothes' during an address to the European Football Clubs. Ceferin declared it is time to say enough to Fifa while citing the failed FFE project and the Folarin Balogun affair.

content:
Spain took an early lead against Croatia in a UEFA Nations League match in Seville, with Lamine Yamal scoring within seconds of kickoff. The Spanish forward received the ball on the edge of the area after a move from left to right and finished with a first-time shot. This contest marked Spain’s first home game since winning the World Cup for the second time.

Unai Simón served as the captain for Spain, while Ivan Perisic, aged 37, led the Croatian side. The match was part of a series of Nations League updates featuring 7.45pm BST kick-offs, which also included a fixture between Czechia and England.

title: James Trafford defends Manchester City season with two trophies
content:
James Trafford, the Leeds United goalkeeper, defended his recent season at Manchester City by stating, “I won two trophies,” when asked if it had been a wasted year. The goalkeeper was thrust into the England lineup for only his third cap during a Nations League match against Spain at Wembley on Saturday.

During the opening 35 minutes of that match, Trafford made two excellent saves to keep England in contention while facing pressure from the world champions. His performance helped lay the groundwork for a 2-1 half-time lead for England.

Despite the early advantage, England ultimately lost the Nations League opener 3-2 after Harry Kane missed a penalty in the 54th minute. The current Nations League fixture between Czechia and England is scheduled to kick off at 7.45pm BST in Prague.
summary: James Trafford firmly stated he won two trophies at Manchester City, rejecting the idea that his season was a waste. He recently made two excellent saves for England in their 3-2 Nations League loss to Spain.
